name: Hitachi
location: On the Pacific coast of north-east Ibaraki Prefecture, serving the industrial area centred on the city of Hitachi, north-east of Tokyo.
summary: Hitachi opened in 1959 and since 2008 has been one of three districts of the Port of Ibaraki, alongside Hitachinaka and Oarai. It is a mixed cargo port with five wharves and 14 public berths, and finished vehicles are among its main cargoes. Total throughput reached a record of about 8.74 million tonnes in 2023.
vehicleHandling: Wharves 3 and 5 handle finished vehicles. The district is Mercedes-Benz's largest import hub in Japan and Nissan's export base for North American shipments from its Tochigi plant, and Wharf 3 has what the city describes as Japan's largest motor pool. In 2025 Hitachi ranked third among Japanese ports for imported vehicles, with 33,057 units.
hinterland: The northern Kanto region, including Ibaraki and neighbouring Tochigi Prefecture.

name: Kobe
location: On Osaka Bay in Hyogo Prefecture, in the Keihanshin (Osaka, Kyoto and Kobe) area of western Japan.
summary: Kobe was the world's busiest container port from 1973 to 1978 and remains one of Japan's main container gateways, with container terminals on the artificial Port Island and Rokko Island. The city reported about 2.77 million TEU in 2024, down 2.2% on 2023.
vehicleHandling: Car carriers are worked at Rokko Island wharf L-2, where stevedores handle cars, large trucks, construction machinery and non-self-propelled cargo on MAFI trailers. Shinko East Pier has a vehicle base with storage for about 2,000 vehicles and an export inspection facility, serving the growing used-car export trade by car carrier and by container.
hinterland: The Kansai region, including Kobe, Osaka and Kyoto.

facts.label: Port manager
facts.value: City of Kobe Port and Harbor Bureau

facts.label: Container berths
facts.value: 34, with a maximum draught of 18 m

name: Nagoya
location: At the head of Ise Bay in Aichi Prefecture, on Japan's Pacific coast, midway between Tokyo and Osaka.
summary: Nagoya is Japan's largest port by total cargo, handling 156.71 million tonnes and 2.76 million TEU in 2024. It has been Japan's leading vehicle export port every year since 1979, reflecting the concentration of the car industry around it.
vehicleHandling: Kinjo Pier is the public export base for finished vehicles, used by Toyota, Honda, Suzuki and Mitsubishi. Shinpo Pier is a Toyota-only export terminal and Yatomi Pier is used by Mitsubishi, while Tobishima Pier is the main container terminal. The port exported 1,482,976 vehicles in 2025, the most of any Japanese port.
hinterland: The Chubu region around Nagoya, the centre of Japan's car manufacturing industry.

facts.label: Vehicle terminals
facts.value: Kinjo Pier (public), Shinpo Pier (Toyota), Yatomi Pier (Mitsubishi)

name: Tomakomai
location: On the Pacific coast of southern Hokkaido, stretching from Tomakomai to Atsuma, about 65 km from Sapporo and 20 km from New Chitose Airport.
summary: Tomakomai opened in 1963 as a coal export port and is known as the world's first large-scale inland excavated port, dug out of dry land and flooded. It is northern Japan's largest trade port, handling about half of Hokkaido's seaborne cargo, and has two areas, the West Port (1963) and the East Port (1980). In 2024 it handled about 100 million tonnes of cargo, its twelfth straight year above 100 million, including 233,455 TEU of international containers.
vehicleHandling: Most of the port's traffic is domestic, and the Hokkaido regional development bureau lists finished vehicles among its main domestic cargoes, carried on the car ferries and RoRo ships that link the West and East Port areas with Honshu ports such as Nagoya, Sendai, Oarai, Hachinohe, Niigata, Akita and Tsuruga. Official port material does not name a dedicated deep-sea car terminal, so vehicles move through the RoRo, ferry and general cargo berths, and containerised cars through the international container terminal.
hinterland: Hokkaido, including Sapporo.

name: Toyohashi
location: On Mikawa Bay in eastern Aichi Prefecture, with Toyohashi at its centre, in central Japan between the Tokyo and Osaka regions.
summary: Toyohashi is the core of Mikawa Port, which has about 20 km of quays and has been Japan's leading port for imported cars by both value and units since 1993. Roughly half of the imported cars sold in Japan are landed here, and Mikawa is also Japan's second-largest vehicle export port.
vehicleHandling: The Jinno district is the main public area, with an East zone of 96 ha and a West zone of 120 ha and 3,790 m of public quays 4 to 12 m deep. The West zone handles finished vehicle exports and hosts import vehicle processing centres for Mercedes-Benz, Volvo, Jaguar Land Rover and Stellantis, while Volkswagen Group Japan uses company berths in the neighbouring Akemi district. In 2025 Mikawa Port handled 184,079 imported and 837,666 exported vehicles.
hinterland: Aichi Prefecture and the Chubu car-making region, with road links towards both Tokyo and Osaka.

name: Yokohama
location: On the western shore of Tokyo Bay in Kanagawa Prefecture, serving the Tokyo metropolitan area.
summary: Yokohama opened to foreign trade in 1859 and is one of Japan's main international ports, with ten major piers including Honmoku, Daikoku and Minami Honmoku. It is also Japan's third-largest vehicle export port by units.
vehicleHandling: Daikoku Pier, a 322 ha artificial island, is the largest vehicle export hub in eastern Japan. Former container berths there have been converted to RoRo car berths, and since works completed in 2022 up to 11 pure car carriers can berth at once, with a 1,400 m continuous quay taking five large carriers. The port exported 833,217 vehicles and imported 24,578 in 2025.
hinterland: Tokyo, Kanagawa and the wider Kanto region.

facts.label: Port manager
facts.value: Port and Harbor Bureau, City of Yokohama

name: Kunsan
location: At the mouth of the Geum River in Gunsan, North Jeolla Province, midway down Korea's west (Yellow Sea) coast.
summary: Gunsan opened as a port to ship grain from the Honam plain and has been expanded since, with a new port developed from the 1990s as trade with China grew. It serves as a gateway for the central west coast and has an international passenger service to Shidao in China.
vehicleHandling: Pier 4 is a dedicated vehicle pier used as a base for Korean car exports, with two 300 m berths for 20,000-tonne ships; GM Korea and CJ Logistics are listed as its cargo owner and stevedore. Pier 5 is a multipurpose pier with eight berths handling cars as well as pulp, grain and logs, and Pier 6 has a container terminal.
hinterland: North Jeolla Province and the Honam region of south-west Korea.

facts.label: Owner and manager
facts.value: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Gunsan Regional Office

facts.label: Multipurpose pier
facts.value: Pier 5, eight berths, cars and general cargo

name: Masan
location: In Changwon, South Gyeongsang Province, on a sheltered ria inlet of Korea's south-east coast.
summary: Masan opened as a trading port in 1899 and handles steel, vehicles, machinery and cement for the surrounding industrial region. It has 37 berths and capacity for more than 10 million tonnes of cargo a year.
vehicleHandling: Pier 4, with seven 20,000-tonne berths along 1,050 m of quay at 11 m depth, is run as a dedicated container and vehicle pier and is the port's car export facility. The Gapo New Port terminal, four berths along 980 m at 12 m depth, also handles containers, general cargo and vehicles.
hinterland: Changwon and the South Gyeongsang industrial region, linked by the Namhae and Guma expressways.

facts.value: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Masan Regional Office

facts.value: Gapo New Port, 980 m, 12 m depth

name: Pyeongtaek
location: On Asan Bay on Korea's west coast, straddling Pyeongtaek in Gyeonggi Province and Dangjin in South Chungcheong Province, south of Seoul.
summary: Pyeongtaek-Dangjin is a port built on reclaimed land inside Asan Bay, sheltered from typhoons and storm surges, with an average depth of about 14 m. It is the closest major Korean port to China's coastal industrial belt, and Seoul, Incheon, Suwon, Cheonan, Cheongju and Daejeon all lie within about 80 km.
vehicleHandling: Berths 1 to 5 on the East Pier are vehicle berths, including dedicated car berths 2 and 3 (completed in 2008 and 2010) and the Kia car pier at berths 4 and 5 (2007). They take ships of 30,000 to 50,000 tonnes and are backed by 160,000 to 225,000 square metres of yard per berth group. The East Pier also has the port's container berths.
hinterland: Seoul and the capital region, plus the central region around Cheonan, Cheongju and Daejeon.

facts.label: Manager
facts.value: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Pyeongtaek Regional Office

facts.label: Dedicated car berths
facts.value: Berths 2 and 3; Kia pier at berths 4 and 5

name: Busan
location: At the south-eastern tip of the Korean peninsula in Busan, facing the Korea Strait.
summary: Busan is South Korea's largest port and a major transhipment hub for North-East Asia. It handled a record 24.88 million TEU in 2025, up 2% on 24.4 million TEU in 2024, with transhipment making up about 57%. It is made up of the North Port, the highly automated New Port, Gamcheon and Dadaepo.
vehicleHandling: Busan is built around container handling and has no dedicated car terminal. Car carriers do call at Busan New Port, where the port's New Port Multipurpose Terminal (700 m of quay at 15 m depth, run by Busan New Port Multipurpose Terminal Co.) handles non-container cargo, and Renault Korea's Busan-built cars have been exported through the New Port. General cargo is also worked at North Port Pier 7 and the Gamcheon Central Pier, and cars shipped in containers go through the container terminals.
hinterland: South-eastern Korea around Busan, plus transhipment cargo moving through North-East Asia.

facts.label: Multipurpose terminal
facts.value: Busan New Port Multipurpose Terminal, 700 m, 15 m depth

name: Keelung
location: In Keelung City on the northern tip of Taiwan, the main seaport for the Taipei area.
summary: Keelung is one of Taiwan's international commercial ports and the main seaport for northern Taiwan, developed as a modern port under Japanese rule from 1899. It handled about 1.60 million TEU in 2025, down slightly from 1.65 million TEU in 2024. It is also Taiwan's main cruise home port.
vehicleHandling: Keelung has no dedicated car terminal. The port company lists 19 general cargo wharves that are used for cars, yachts and steel, alongside 13 container wharves, and vehicles are handled across these. The same branch also manages the nearby Port of Taipei, whose East Wharf area hosts automotive logistics businesses.
hinterland: Taipei and the rest of northern Taiwan.

facts.label: Operator
facts.value: Taiwan International Ports Corporation, Keelung Branch

name: Taichung
location: In Wuqi District, Taichung, on Taiwan's west coast facing the Taiwan Strait, roughly equidistant from Keelung and Kaohsiung.
summary: Taichung opened in 1976 as one of Taiwan's Ten Major Construction Projects and is now the country's second-largest port by cargo and third by containers. It covers 11,285 ha, has 64 berths and can take bulk ships of up to 206,000 tonnes.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled in the Middle Wharf area, where berths 16 to 19 are backed by bonded car warehouses leased by Volkswagen and by a vehicle storage and transfer operator. Berth 18 is a 360 m passenger and cargo wharf with 11 m depth.
hinterland: Central Taiwan.

facts.label: Operator
facts.value: Taiwan International Ports Corporation, Taichung Branch

name: Hong Kong
location: On the South China Sea at the mouth of the Pearl River, with its main container terminals at Kwai Chung and Tsing Yi.
summary: Hong Kong is one of the world's major container ports, though volumes have fallen from about 24.4 million TEU in 2011 to about 13.0 million TEU in 2025. The Kwai Tsing terminals handled about 9.7 million TEU of that, around 74%, with the rest moving through mid-stream sites and other wharves. It remains a hub for cargo moving between the Pearl River Delta and the rest of the world.
vehicleHandling: The port's official material does not describe any RoRo or car-carrier facility. Hong Kong is built around the nine Kwai Tsing container terminals, with 24 berths run by five operators including Modern Terminals, Hongkong International Terminals and COSCO, none of which is a dedicated vehicle terminal. Cargo also moves through the River Trade Terminal at Tuen Mun and the Marine Department's public cargo working areas.
hinterland: Hong Kong itself and the Pearl River Delta region of southern China.

facts.value: Marine Department, Hong Kong SAR Government

facts.value: About 9.7 million TEU, 74% of the port (2025)

facts.value: 12.5 to 15.5 m at the container terminals

name: Macau
location: On the western side of the Pearl River estuary, with its only deep-water cargo port at Ka Ho on the north-east of Coloane.
summary: Macau has a single deep-water harbour, at Ka Ho, which holds the Macau Container Terminal, a fuel oil wharf and wharves for the cement works and the power company. The historic Inner Harbour has a fairway only about 3.5 m deep and is used by small vessels, including container feeders to and from Hong Kong.
vehicleHandling: Macau has no RoRo or dedicated vehicle terminal, so cars arrive in containers rather than on car carriers. The Ka Ho container terminal, opened in 1991, has two berths of 135 m and 171.4 m, and most container cargo reaches Macau on daily feeder services from Hong Kong, for example Macau Hong Kong Terminal's service from Hong Kong's Stonecutters Island to its 152 m Inner Harbour terminal. Containers can also come by road from Hong Kong over the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge, through a cross-border cargo transfer station at the Macau port of entry.

facts.value: Daily container feeders from Hong Kong

name: Chittagong (Chattogram)
location: On the Karnaphuli River at Chattogram, near its mouth on the Bay of Bengal in south-east Bangladesh.
summary: Bangladesh's principal seaport, run by the Chittagong Port Authority, and the busiest container port on the Bay of Bengal. It handled a record 3.41 million TEU in calendar 2025, up 4.1% from about 3.28 million TEU in 2024, along with about 138 million tonnes of cargo and 4,273 ship calls. River draft limits restrict the size of ships that can come alongside.
vehicleHandling: There is no dedicated car terminal. Car carriers discharge at the port's general cargo jetties, for example jetties 7 and 8 in 2023, and imported vehicles are held in the port's car sheds until delivery, which have at times filled up and kept car carriers waiting at anchor in busy periods. About 24,150 cars were imported through the port in 2023, down from 61,467 in 2019, as importers moved much of the reconditioned car trade to Mongla. Containerised cars go through the container terminals: New Mooring, Chittagong Container Terminal and the Patenga Container Terminal, which began operating in June 2024.
hinterland: Handles more than 90% of Bangladesh's general cargo and nearly all its containerised trade.

facts.label: Container terminals
facts.value: New Mooring, Chittagong Container Terminal, Patenga Container Terminal

name: Muara
location: At Muara in the Brunei-Muara District on Brunei Bay, about 28 km from the capital, Bandar Seri Begawan.
summary: Brunei's largest port, opened for commercial operations in 1973. Since July 2018 it has been run by Muara Port Company, a joint venture between Brunei's Darussalam Assets and China's Guangxi Beibu Gulf International Port Group, under the Maritime and Port Authority of Brunei Darussalam. Most of its throughput is imports, with vehicles and manufactured goods among the main cargoes.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled at the Muara Conventional Terminal, which takes non-containerised cargo such as break bulk, vehicles and livestock over 611 m of berths with up to 12.5 m draught, backed by 5 hectares of open storage and three transit sheds. RoRo ships berth at this conventional terminal rather than at a dedicated RoRo terminal. Containerised cars go through the Muara Container Terminal, which has a 250 m berth, 12.5 m draught and a capacity of about 220,000 TEU a year; a new container terminal due in 2027 is intended to raise capacity to about 500,000 TEU.
hinterland: Serves Brunei, including Bandar Seri Begawan, and parts of Sabah and Sarawak.

facts.value: Muara Port Company (Darussalam Assets and Beibu Gulf International Port Group)

facts.value: Maritime and Port Authority of Brunei Darussalam

name: Ennore (Kamarajar Port)
location: On the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal at Ennore, in the northern part of Chennai, about 18 km north of Chennai Port.
summary: Commissioned in February 2001, Kamarajar Port was the first major port in India to be run as a public company. It handled about 49 million tonnes of cargo in 2025-26 and 671,393 TEU of containers in 2023-24, with a permissible draft of 13.5 metres.
vehicleHandling: A dedicated RoRo car terminal opened in 2011 to serve vehicle exports from the Chennai and Bengaluru manufacturing cluster, backed by parking yards for about 10,000, 5,000 and 2,500 cars. Car volumes rose from about 54,000 in 2010-11 to about 215,000 in 2014-15, and the port handled about 191,000 export vehicles in 2025-26. It has berthed pure car and truck carriers of more than 9,000 car-equivalent units and, in 2025, became the first Indian port to handle automobile transhipment.
hinterland: The Chennai and Bengaluru automotive belt in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, plus plants in southern Andhra Pradesh such as Sri City.

name: Mumbai
location: In Mumbai Harbour on India's west coast in Maharashtra, a natural deep-water harbour sheltered between Mumbai island and the Konkan mainland.
summary: One of India's oldest ports, set up as the Bombay Port Trust in 1873 and run by the Mumbai Port Authority since 2022. It handled about 68.6 million tonnes in 2024-25, mostly bulk and petroleum products. Most container traffic for the Mumbai region has been handled at the nearby Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva) since 1989.
vehicleHandling: Car carriers use the Offshore Container Terminal (OCT), two berths with 700 m of quay reached by a trestle from Indira Dock, which the port authority says now handles RoRo vessels and car carriers for car and steel exports. The berths are licensed to Indira Container Terminal Pvt Ltd and have handled RoRo ships since July 2015, with the berth pocket kept at 11 m. The traffic is mainly exports: Škoda Auto Volkswagen India alone shipped more than 40,000 vehicles through the port in 2025-26. Cars shipped in containers to Mumbai generally go through Jawaharlal Nehru Port.
hinterland: Mumbai and the vehicle manufacturing hubs of Pune and Nashik in Maharashtra.

name: Pipavav
location: On the Saurashtra coast of Gujarat on India's west coast, about 152 nautical miles (roughly 10 hours' steaming) north-west of Nhava Sheva.
summary: India's first public-private partnership port, operated by APM Terminals through Gujarat Pipavav Port Ltd. It handles containers (capacity about 1.35 million TEU a year), dry and liquid bulk and vehicles, with a maximum draft of 14.5 metres.
vehicleHandling: A dedicated RoRo yard, developed with NYK Auto Logistics and opened in 2015, can handle about 250,000 vehicles a year and has a stockyard for about 6,000 cars plus a pre-delivery inspection facility. Many cars arrive by rail on dedicated vehicle rakes; in May 2024 the port unloaded 40 such rakes carrying 3,969 vehicles, a monthly record. Container services use eight post-Panamax quay cranes.
hinterland: North-west India, including Gujarat's vehicle plants, connected by road and by rail via the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor.

facts.value: RoRo yard with NYK Auto Logistics, about 250,000 vehicles a year

facts.label: Rail
facts.value: 11 sidings, up to 12 trains a day

name: Jakarta (Tanjung Priok)
location: In North Jakarta on the Java Sea coast, serving Indonesia's capital.
summary: Indonesia's busiest and most advanced seaport, operated by the state-owned Pelindo. It handled about 7.6 million TEU in 2024 across its container terminals, which include Jakarta International Container Terminal, Koja, New Priok Container Terminal One and Terminal 3.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles go through a dedicated car terminal run by PT Indonesia Kendaraan Terminal (IPC Car Terminal, IPCC), a Pelindo subsidiary set up in 2012, which handles RoRo imports, exports and domestic traffic. In 2025 its Tanjung Priok site covered about 18.9 hectares with a capacity of about 12,000 vehicle units, and it handled more than 100,000 battery electric vehicles that year. Containerised cars go through the port's container terminals.
hinterland: Greater Jakarta and western Java, Indonesia's largest consumer and manufacturing region.

facts.label: Vehicle terminal
facts.value: IPC Car Terminal (PT Indonesia Kendaraan Terminal Tbk)

name: Port Klang
location: In the Klang District of Selangor on the Strait of Malacca, about 38 km south-west of Kuala Lumpur.
summary: Malaysia's largest port, opened as Port Swettenham in 1901 and renamed in 1972. It handled a record 15.14 million TEU in 2025 and has three main areas: Westports on Pulau Indah, Northport and Southpoint.
vehicleHandling: Both Westports and Northport handle RoRo vehicles alongside containers and conventional cargo. At Westports, a vehicle terminal facility operated by Toyofuji Logistics Malaysia opened in 2008, and the port had handled a cumulative 3 million cars from its RoRo operations by December 2023. Westports alone handled about 11.3 million TEU in 2025.
hinterland: Kuala Lumpur, the Klang Valley and peninsular Malaysia.

facts.label: Westports RoRo
facts.value: 3 million cars handled cumulatively by December 2023

name: Malé
location: At the north-west corner of Malé island, the capital of the Maldives, in the Indian Ocean.
summary: The main port of the Maldives and its principal international maritime gateway, operated by Maldives Ports Limited. Space is very limited, and unloading a ship has typically taken five to seven days. The government plans to move most commercial port services to a new port at Thilafushi by November 2027.
vehicleHandling: There is no dedicated RoRo or vehicle terminal. The main berth has about 102 metres of quay with a depth of 9.25 metres, supported by barge quays and lighterage berths, and some ships are worked at anchor with cargo brought ashore by lighter. The port has about 21,700 square metres of open storage, reach stackers, RTG cranes and mobile cranes of up to 160 tonnes.
hinterland: Malé and the wider Maldives, with cargo moved on to other islands by domestic vessels.

name: Karachi
location: At Karachi on the Arabian Sea coast of Sindh, in southern Pakistan.
summary: Pakistan's largest deep-water port, managed by the Karachi Port Trust, which dates from 1887. It handled a record 54 million tonnes of cargo and 2.65 million TEU in the 2024-25 financial year across about 40 berths on its East, West and South Wharves.
vehicleHandling: There is no dedicated car terminal. The container terminals are Karachi Gateway Terminal (AD Ports, East Wharf), Karachi International Container Terminal (Hutchison Ports, West Wharf) and South Asia Pakistan Terminals (Hutchison Ports, South Wharf, 18 m draft). In July 2026 the car carrier Grande Shanghai discharged more than 2,000 electric vehicles at the Karachi Gateway Terminal Multipurpose berths (11 to 17), reported as Pakistan's first RoRo vehicle import.
hinterland: Karachi, Sindh and the rest of Pakistan; the port handles more than half of the country's foreign trade.

facts.label: Container terminals
facts.value: KGTL (AD Ports), KICT and SAPT (Hutchison Ports)

name: Colombo
location: On the west coast of Sri Lanka at Colombo, the country's principal city, close to the main east-west shipping lanes across the Indian Ocean.
summary: Sri Lanka's largest port and a major transhipment hub for South Asia, run by the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA). It handled a record 8.29 million TEU in 2025, up from 7.79 million TEU in 2024. Container terminals include SLPA's Jaya and Unity terminals, South Asia Gateway Terminals and Colombo International Container Terminals.
vehicleHandling: There is no dedicated car terminal. SLPA's 2019 port development plan noted that the shallow Unity Container Terminal (9 m) was often used for RoRo cargo and that most RoRo imports and transhipment had moved to Hambantota, which has more space. General cargo is worked at Bandaranaike Quay, and SLPA handles containerised vehicles under separate RoRo manifests.
hinterland: Colombo and the rest of Sri Lanka, plus transhipment cargo for India and the wider region.

name: Laem Chabang
location: In Chonburi Province on the eastern shore of the Gulf of Thailand, about 130 km south-east of Bangkok.
summary: Thailand's largest port, owned by the Port Authority of Thailand and opened in 1991, with terminals leased to private operators. It handled more than 10 million TEU in 2025. A third phase, with 18-metre berths for the largest container ships, is under construction.
vehicleHandling: Cars are handled at the dedicated A5 RoRo terminal, operated by Namyong Terminal, which has three wharves of about 697 metres, about 78 hectares of storage (space for about 49,000 vehicles) and capacity for about 1.2 million vehicles a year. Namyong's concession expired on 30 April 2026 and it is running the terminal on a temporary basis while the Port Authority of Thailand selects a new operator. Containerised cars go through the container terminals in Basins 1 and 2.
hinterland: Bangkok and central and eastern Thailand, including the Eastern Seaboard industrial and car-making zones.

facts.label: Vehicle terminal
facts.value: A5 RoRo terminal (Namyong Terminal, temporary operation since May 2026)

name: Singapore
location: On the southern coast of the island of Singapore, at the southern end of the Strait of Malacca.
summary: The world's second-busiest container port and a leading transhipment hub, handling 44.66 million TEU in 2025. PSA Singapore runs the container terminals at Tanjong Pagar, Keppel, Brani, Pasir Panjang and the new Tuas Port (opened September 2022), while Jurong Port handles bulk and conventional cargo.
vehicleHandling: Cars go through the Pasir Panjang Automobile Terminal, Singapore's first dedicated car terminal, which opened in January 2009 with three berths and an open yard plus a multi-storey car park, about 20,000 lots in all. Asia Automobile Terminal Singapore, a PSA, NYK and K Line joint venture there (extended for 12 years in May 2024), has two deep-water RoRo berths and capacity for about 1 million vehicles a year, making it South-East Asia's largest vehicle transhipment hub.
hinterland: Singapore itself; most vehicle traffic is transhipment between Asian producers and markets in Europe, Africa and the Middle East.

facts.label: Port authority
facts.value: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore

name: Shanghai
location: At the mouth of the Yangtze River on China's east coast, facing the East China Sea and Hangzhou Bay, with the offshore Yangshan deep-water port linked to the mainland by the Donghai Bridge.
summary: The world's busiest container port every year since 2010, handling 55.06 million TEU in 2025. It is operated mainly by Shanghai International Port Group (SIPG). In 2024 it also became the world's largest vehicle port for the first time, handling 3.63 million vehicles by RoRo.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled by Haitong International Automotive Terminal, whose main site at Waigaoqiao holds about 40,000 vehicles, handles more than 7,000 a day and exported 1.3 million vehicles in 2024. A second RoRo terminal at Yangshan's southern port area handled more than 370,000 vehicles in 2024, and a new Haitong terminal at Taicang in Jiangsu opened in December 2024. The port has RoRo links to about 289 ports in 131 countries and regions.
hinterland: Shanghai and the Yangtze River Delta, China's largest car-making region, with feeder links up the Yangtze.

name: Xingang (Tianjin)
location: On the western shore of Bohai Bay at the mouth of the Hai River, about 60 km east of central Tianjin and 170 km south-east of Beijing.
summary: The largest port in northern China and the main seaport for Beijing, run by the state-owned Tianjin Port Group. It is spread over several port areas, with Beijiang, Nanjiang and Dongjiang at its core around the main fairway.
vehicleHandling: Tianjin is northern China's largest vehicle import and export hub, with more than 30 RoRo routes to Europe, the Middle East and South America; it exported about 640,000 vehicles in 2024. RoRo traffic is handled by Tianjin Port Global Ro-Ro Terminal, which in August 2026 opened a new yard in the Beijiang port area with about 5,000 spaces, including multi-storey parking, and capacity for about 140,000 vehicles a year. A single ship loaded more than 4,000 vehicles in March 2025, a port record.
hinterland: Beijing, Tianjin and Hebei, which together form a major car-making cluster, plus inland northern China, with rail links towards Central Asia.

name: Xinsha (Guangzhou)
location: At Machong Town in Dongguan, Guangdong, on the Pearl River in the Pearl River Delta; it is one of the port areas of Guangzhou Port.
summary: Opened in December 1992 and run by Guangzhou Port Xinsha Port Affairs Co., a Guangzhou Port Group company. It handles coal, grain, containers and vehicles, with more than 73 million tonnes of cargo a year and a maximum depth of 13.5 metres.
vehicleHandling: Xinsha has handled RoRo vehicle imports since 2006 and is promoted as a South China car RoRo hub; Guangzhou Port's other main car terminal is at Nansha. Since 2024, GAC export cars have been brought down the river from Longsha by RoRo vessel for export through Xinsha. Foreign-trade car exports at Xinsha rose by about 170% year on year in the first half of 2026.
hinterland: Guangzhou, Dongguan and the wider Pearl River Delta manufacturing region, including GAC's car plants.

facts.label: Operator
facts.value: Guangzhou Port Xinsha Port Affairs Co. (Guangzhou Port Group)

name: Yantai
location: At Yantai on the northern coast of the Shandong Peninsula, on the Yellow Sea in eastern China.
summary: A large Shandong port, part of Shandong Port Group, handling bulk cargo, containers, liquid bulk, vehicles and passenger and cargo RoRo ferries. Around 40 berths were added between 2001 and 2005, and by December 2011 it had become the tenth Chinese port to handle 200 million tonnes of cargo in a year.
vehicleHandling: Yantai handles vehicle exports by RoRo ship, including from the Zhifu Bay port area. It handled about 288,000 vehicles in the first five months of 2024, up about 30% on the year before, and had 14 vehicle routes reaching more than 30 countries and regions.
hinterland: Shandong province and northern China.

name: St John's
location: On the north-west coast of Antigua, in the capital St John's.
summary: St John's Deep Water Harbour is the largest port in Antigua and Barbuda and the country's only port with berths for international cargo ships. It is run by the Antigua and Barbuda Port Authority and was rebuilt between January 2018 and December 2022 by China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation, financed by a concessional loan from the Export-Import Bank of China. The rebuilt port can berth two 10,000-tonne ships at the same time and has a design capacity of 550,000 tonnes of cargo a year.
vehicleHandling: Port sources describe no separate ro-ro terminal, so vehicles are landed at the multipurpose cargo berths, where the harbour has a draught of 35 ft (about 11 m). The port is served by ro-ro feeder ships: Höegh Autoliners lists St John's among the destinations of its Caribbean shortsea service, which connects to its deep-sea car carriers through Caribbean hubs.
hinterland: Serves Antigua, and the government positions the rebuilt port as a logistics and transhipment hub for the north-eastern Caribbean.

name: Oranjestad
fullName: Port of Oranjestad and Barcadera Terminal
location: On the south-west coast of Aruba; the Oranjestad harbour is in the capital and the Barcadera cargo terminal is about 5 km to the south-east.
summary: Oranjestad is Aruba's capital and main cruise port, and the name carriers use for Aruba. Container and general cargo moved out of the town harbour to the purpose-built Barcadera terminal, which officially opened on 12 April 2016. Both are under the Aruba Ports Authority.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled at Barcadera, where the Aruba Ports Authority lists vehicles among the break-bulk cargo alongside containers, yachts and heavy equipment. The terminal is run by Aruba Stevedoring Company (ASTEC), a private company, and has a 440 m quay with 11 m of water alongside and 40 reefer positions.
hinterland: Serves the island of Aruba.

name: Nassau
location: On Arawak Cay at the mouth of Nassau Harbour, about two miles west of downtown Nassau on New Providence.
summary: Nassau Container Port is the main commercial port for New Providence, opened in 2011 and owned and run by APD Limited (Arawak Port Development). APD is a public-private partnership: 40% is owned by the Bahamas government, 40% by a consortium of shipping investors and 20% by Bahamian members of the public. In the 12 months to June 2025 the port handled 73,084 TEU, 3.3% more than the year before.
vehicleHandling: APD does not describe a dedicated ro-ro terminal, so vehicles are landed across its container and break-bulk terminals on Arawak Cay; around 19,300 vehicles arrived there in the 12 months to June 2025, 2.3% fewer than the year before. The break-bulk terminal has 600 ft of berth at 21 ft, and the container terminal has three berths at 28 ft worked by three 320-tonne Liebherr mobile harbour cranes. Höegh Autoliners lists Nassau among the destinations of its Caribbean ro-ro feeder service.
hinterland: Serves New Providence, the most populous island of the Bahamas.

name: Bridgetown
location: On the south-west coast of Barbados, just north-west of central Bridgetown in St Michael.
summary: Bridgetown Port, officially the Deep Water Harbour, is Barbados's main seaport and handles about 90% of the goods used by the island's manufacturing and retail sectors. It is run by Barbados Port Inc., a statutory corporation, and combines a container and cargo terminal with a cruise port. Barbados handled 101,300 TEU in 2023, against a peak of about 107,100 TEU in 2017.
vehicleHandling: Barbados Port Inc. does not list a dedicated ro-ro berth; containers and break-bulk are worked at the multipurpose Berths 3 to 6, which also take cruise ships, and inter-island break-bulk ships use the 156 m Shallow Draught berth. Berth 6 is the largest at 313 m with 12 m of water. Ro-ro feeder ships do call: Höegh Autoliners lists Bridgetown among the destinations of its Caribbean shortsea service.
hinterland: Serves the whole of Barbados, handling most imports for manufacturing and retail.

facts.label: Cargo berths
facts.value: Berths 3 to 6 (150 to 313 m, 11 to 12 m depth)

name: Hamilton
location: On Front Street in the City of Hamilton, on Hamilton Harbour in central Bermuda.
summary: Hamilton's freight docks are Bermuda's main cargo port and sit beside the city's cruise berths. The docks are owned and managed by the Corporation of Hamilton, and cargo handling is contracted to a private stevedoring company, Stevedoring Services. The docks handled around 35,000 containers a year according to a 2022 report.
vehicleHandling: Cars reach Hamilton mainly on Bermuda Container Line's weekly service from Port Elizabeth, New Jersey. Its MV Oleander, built in 2019, is a combined container and ro-ro ship carrying 456 TEU plus 113 cars in an enclosed garage.
hinterland: Serves the whole of Bermuda, supplying almost all of the island's imported goods.

name: George Town
location: On Harbour Drive in George Town, on the west coast of Grand Cayman.
summary: The Port of George Town is the main cargo and cruise port of the Cayman Islands, run by the Port Authority of the Cayman Islands, a statutory body set up in 1976. It is a compact facility for ships up to 122 m long and 5.5 m draught, and cargo is stored at the authority's Cargo Distribution Centre on Portland Road, which has 13 acres of open storage and room for about 1,800 TEU. In 2024 the port handled 73,013 TEU and 374,134 tons of imported cargo (excluding aggregate), both slightly down on 2023.
vehicleHandling: George Town has a dedicated ro-ro berth, the North Cargo Pier, which is 200 ft long with 19 to 26 ft of water, while containers are lifted at the South Cargo Pier (440 ft) and the West Wall (525 ft). There are no ship-to-shore gantries; the port has two 100,000 lb dock cranes. Höegh Autoliners lists Georgetown, Grand Cayman among the destinations of its Caribbean ro-ro feeder service.
hinterland: Serves Grand Cayman, with freight for Cayman Brac and Little Cayman moving on by local shipping.

name: Willemstad
location: In Willemstad on the south coast of Curaçao, reached through the St Anna Bay channel into the Schottegat inner harbour.
summary: Willemstad is Curaçao's main and largest port, built around the St Anna Bay entrance and the Schottegat, a 60-hectare natural inner bay. The Schottegat holds the container terminal, cargo wharves, a large dry dock and the island's refinery. The port is overseen by Curaçao Ports Authority.
vehicleHandling: The container terminal is run by Curaçao Port Services (CPS) under a concession from Curaçao Ports Authority and has a ro-ro berth beside the gantry crane rail, so ro-ro and lift-on operations can run together. It has 12.2 m of water and two 50-tonne gantry cranes. Vehicles are also handled at Brion Wharf, a general cargo quay of about 879 m.
hinterland: Serves Curaçao.

name: Roseau
location: At Woodbridge Bay, about 2 km north of Roseau on the south-west coast of Dominica.
summary: Woodbridge Bay is Dominica's main port of entry and its principal cargo port, run entirely by the Dominica Air and Sea Ports Authority (DASPA) with no private operator. The main pier dates from 1976 and the Logistics Cluster assessment notes it needs heavy reinvestment. The port handled about 15,000 TEU in 2017.
vehicleHandling: Cars arrive at the general cargo and container wharf, where ro-ro and lift-on cargo share the two berths. The main wharf is 244 m long with a minimum of 10 m alongside, plus a 91 m extension at 7.9 m. There are no shore cranes, so ships must use their own gear; DASPA does all loading and handling.
hinterland: Serves the whole of Dominica.

facts.value: Dominica Air and Sea Ports Authority (DASPA)

name: Manzanillo
location: At Pepillo Salcedo on Manzanillo Bay in Montecristi province, on the north-west coast of the Dominican Republic next to the Haitian border.
summary: Manzanillo was built in the 1950s by the Grenada Company, a US fruit company, to export bananas, and fruit exports remain its main trade alongside clinker, cement and general cargo. The Dominican Port Authority is rebuilding it as a combined cargo and cruise port, with Inter-American Development Bank financing of more than US$100 million. In September 2026 the government put physical progress at 52.9%, with the cargo terminal due in the first quarter of 2027.
vehicleHandling: No dedicated ro-ro or vehicle facility is documented at present, and the port mainly handles bananas and bulk cargo with occasional container calls. The new terminal includes a 242 m berth reached by a 183 m access bridge; the associated road from Navarrete has already been completed.
hinterland: Serves the north-west of the Dominican Republic, and the new port is intended to support exports from the free trade zones of Santiago, Moca and La Vega.

facts.value: Inter-American Development Bank, over US$100 million

name: Santo Domingo
location: At the mouth of the Ozama River in central Santo Domingo, on the south coast of the Dominican Republic.
summary: The Port of Santo Domingo sits next to the capital's Colonial City and combines two cruise terminals, Don Diego and Sans Souci, with multipurpose cargo berths. It is administered by the Dominican Port Authority and has been operated under concession by Sansouci Ports since 2005. Sansouci reports about 1,854 m of berthing line and an average of more than 40,000 TEU a year.
vehicleHandling: Santo Domingo is the country's main vehicle-handling port: Sansouci says it receives more than 70,000 ro-ro units a year and is the only Dominican operator with a terminal operating system built for ro-ro cargo. It has a dedicated vehicle warehouse for more than 7,000 units, run with Fast Auto Logistics. Water depth is about 32 ft (9.7 m).
hinterland: Serves Santo Domingo and the southern Dominican Republic.

name: St George's
location: In St George's harbour on the south-west coast of Grenada.
summary: St George's is Grenada's main port, run by the Grenada Ports Authority, which also provides all cargo handling. Cruise ships were moved to the separate Melville Street Cruise Terminal, so cargo and cruise traffic no longer share berths. Grenada's container traffic was 20,299 TEU in 2022.
vehicleHandling: The Grenada Ports Authority does not list a dedicated ro-ro terminal, so vehicles come over the single 335 m main cargo quay on the Carenage, which has 8.3 to 9.8 m of water and takes ships up to 183 m long. Containers are handled with reach stackers and a top lifter rather than shore cranes, and there is a schooner berth for inter-island traffic. Höegh Autoliners lists St George's among the destinations of its Caribbean ro-ro feeder service.
hinterland: Serves Grenada, with inter-island links to Carriacou and Petite Martinique.

name: Pointe-à-Pitre
location: On the Petit Cul-de-Sac Marin in central Guadeloupe, with passenger berths at Pointe-à-Pitre and the cargo port at Jarry in neighbouring Baie-Mahault.
summary: Guadeloupe's port is run by the Grand Port Maritime de la Guadeloupe, trading as Guadeloupe Port Caraïbes, a French state port with five sites across the archipelago. Pointe-à-Pitre handles cruise and inter-island passengers, while Jarry handles about 97% of freight. In 2024 the port handled 3.4 million tonnes and 193,000 TEU.
vehicleHandling: Cars are handled at Jarry, which has nine specialised quays including a dedicated ro-ro berth, container gantry cranes and 15 m of water. A €45 million extension of quay 12 by 120 m, to 280 m, began in 2024, and three new ship-to-shore cranes were being delivered in 2025.
hinterland: Serves Guadeloupe and its dependencies, and the port is developing transhipment to neighbouring islands.

name: Kingston
location: On Kingston Harbour, a large natural harbour on Jamaica's south coast, sheltered by the Palisadoes peninsula.
summary: Kingston is Jamaica's main port and one of the largest transhipment hubs in the Caribbean. The Port Authority of Jamaica is landlord of Kingston Container Terminal, which CMA CGM's Kingston Freeport Terminal Limited has run under a 30-year concession since 1 July 2016, with capacity of 2.8 million TEU. Next to it, Kingston Wharves Limited runs a multi-cargo terminal at Newport West.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled mainly at Kingston Wharves, which has nine berths on 1,655 m of continuous quay and describes itself as the region's leading automotive hub. In mid-2025 it reported transhipping more than 170,000 vehicles in the previous year to 45 destinations, and it is building a multi-storey car park for 10,000 CEU next to the Newport West terminal.
hinterland: Serves the Kingston area and most of Jamaica, and acts as a transhipment hub for vehicles and containers across the Caribbean and beyond.

name: Fort-de-France
location: On the Bay of Fort-de-France on the west coast of Martinique, in the island's capital.
summary: Fort-de-France is Martinique's main port, run by the Grand Port Maritime de la Martinique, a French state port. Its Pointe des Grives container terminal has been named Best Container Port of the Caribbean twice by the Caribbean Shipping Association. In 2024 the port handled 3.18 million tonnes and 187,666 TEU.
vehicleHandling: Ro-ro traffic uses a ro-ro zone with vehicle parking in the Hydrobase east sector, which has 640 m of quay and 11 to 12 m of water. Containers go through Pointe des Grives, with 450 m of quay, 14 m of water and three post-panamax cranes; an extension of the terminal was under way in 2026. Imports of vehicles fell by about 16% in number in 2024.
hinterland: Serves Martinique, with some container transhipment to neighbouring islands.

name: San Juan
location: On San Juan Bay on the north coast of Puerto Rico, in the capital San Juan.
summary: San Juan is Puerto Rico's main port for both cargo and cruise ships, overseen by the Puerto Rico Ports Authority. Cargo is spread across several terminals, chiefly the public Puerto Nuevo zone and the private Isla Grande terminal, and the port handles containers, break-bulk, ro-ro vehicles and bulk fuel. Navigable depths range from 36 to 56 ft.
vehicleHandling: Crowley's 85-acre Isla Grande Terminal takes container and ro-ro ships from Jacksonville, including LNG-powered ConRo ships that carry about 2,400 TEU and up to 400 vehicles on an enclosed deck. At Puerto Nuevo, Puerto Rico Terminals (part of TOTE) runs a 100-acre facility on Piers J to M with a designated vehicle area and 815 m of berth.
hinterland: Serves the whole of Puerto Rico, which receives most of its imports through San Juan.

name: Philipsburg
location: On Great Bay at Philipsburg, on the south coast of the Dutch side of St Martin.
summary: Port St. Maarten at Philipsburg is the island's only deep-water port and one of the Caribbean's busiest cruise ports. Its cargo terminal is a 24-hour multipurpose facility for containers and break-bulk, and it acts as a first port of call and feeder hub for cargo to the surrounding islands. Sint Maarten's container traffic, all of which passes through this port, was 105,200 TEU in 2019, the latest year published by the World Bank.
vehicleHandling: Cars arrive through the multipurpose cargo terminal rather than a dedicated ro-ro facility. The Captain David Cargo Quay is 540 m long with 10.5 m alongside and is worked by Gottwald HMK 260E mobile harbour cranes rated at 100 tonnes, with 3,000 TEU of container storage. Höegh Autoliners' Caribbean ro-ro feeder service lists Philipsburg as a destination.
hinterland: Serves St Martin and acts as a feeder hub for Anguilla, Montserrat, St Barths, St Kitts and Nevis, and Antigua and Barbuda.

summary: The Deep Water Port is the main cargo port of St Kitts, handling container and cargo traffic and transhipments. It is run by the St Christopher Air and Sea Ports Authority (SCASPA), which also runs the Port Zante cruise terminal in central Basseterre. The main berth takes vessels over 900 ft long with a 27 ft draught, and a breasting dolphin built for SCASPA in 2013 and 2014 allows larger ships to berth at the commercial pier.
vehicleHandling: The Deep Water Port has a dedicated ro-ro pier for vessels up to 300 ft, with a minimum depth of 19 ft. Höegh Autoliners lists Basseterre among the destinations of its Caribbean ro-ro feeder service.
hinterland: Serves St Kitts, with Nevis reached by the inter-island ferries from Basseterre.

summary: Port Castries is St Lucia's main port of entry, owned and run by the Saint Lucia Air and Sea Ports Authority (SLASPA), which also manages all stevedoring. It combines downtown cargo berths with cruise berths at Pointe Seraphine and a ferry terminal, and cargo and cruise traffic compete for space in the October to April cruise season. St Lucia's other commercial port is Vieux Fort in the south.

hinterland: Serves St Lucia.

name: Kingstown
location: At Rose Place on the waterfront of Kingstown, on the south-west coast of St Vincent.
summary: Kingstown's new cargo port, built by Aecon on about 6.5 hectares of reclaimed land, replaced the old port facilities and began operating on 25 October 2025. It is run by the St Vincent and the Grenadines Modern Port Operations Company and handles containers, break-bulk, vehicles and personal effects. The container yard has an annual capacity of 53,000 TEU.
vehicleHandling: The new port has a 380 m sheet-pile quay with 12.5 m of water, stern and side ramp access for ro-ro ships, and dedicated open storage for vehicles. Cargo is handled with two mobile harbour cranes and five reach stackers, and there is a container freight station for personal effects.
hinterland: Serves St Vincent and the Grenadines.

name: Port of Spain
location: On the Gulf of Paria in downtown Port of Spain, on the north-west coast of Trinidad.
summary: The Port of Port of Spain is Trinidad and Tobago's main multipurpose port, wholly owned by the government and run by the Port Authority of Trinidad and Tobago. It covers about 142 hectares, 61 of them for cargo, and also hosts the Trinidad to Tobago ferry and cruise ships. The port handled 324,575 TEU in 2024 and 357,820 TEU in 2025, its best result in over a decade.
vehicleHandling: Car carriers are part of the port's regular business, with vehicle storage in a car park and at the Spectrum yard. Containers are worked at Berths 5, 6 and 6A, which have 10.4 to 11.6 m of water, and the port takes ships up to 294 m long with a 12 m maximum draught.
hinterland: Serves Trinidad and Tobago.

name: Mombasa
location: Kilindini Harbour at Mombasa on Kenya's Indian Ocean coast, a natural deep-water inlet that is the country's main international seaport.
summary: Mombasa is Kenya's only international seaport, managed by the Kenya Ports Authority and in use as a harbour since 1896. It handled about 2.11 million TEU and about 45 million tonnes of cargo in 2025, and a large share of its traffic is transit cargo for landlocked neighbours.
vehicleHandling: There is no separate car terminal. The Kenya Ports Authority says multipurpose Berths 1 and 2 take RoRo ships as well as cruise, steel and container vessels, so vehicles on car carriers come in over general berths. Cars shipped in containers go through the port's two container terminals, which have a combined capacity of about 2.3 million TEU a year. Berth 23/19B is planned to raise that to 3.1 million TEU.
hinterland: Mombasa is the start of the Northern Corridor, which carries transit cargo by road, rail and pipeline to Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan and eastern DR Congo.

name: Dar es Salaam
location: A natural harbour in the Kurasini area of Dar es Salaam, Tanzania's largest city, on the Indian Ocean coast.
summary: Dar es Salaam is Tanzania's principal port, owned by the government through the Tanzania Ports Authority and handling around 90 per cent of the country's cargo. It has 11 berths with a total length of over 2,600 metres. Since 2024 most berths have been run by private concessionaires.
vehicleHandling: DP World took over Berths 0 to 7 in April 2024 under a 30-year concession. Berth 0 is a dedicated berth for pure car carriers, with a draught of 12.9 m, and DP World says the switch to pure car and truck carrier operations has cut vehicle discharge times sharply. In early 2026 one vessel discharged 779 car equivalent units in just over 27 hours. Container Terminal 2 is operated separately by Adani International Ports Holdings on a 30-year concession.
hinterland: The port is the gateway for landlocked Zambia, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Rwanda, Burundi and Malawi, linked by road, the TAZARA railway to Zambia and a standard gauge railway under construction towards the Great Lakes.

name: Tamatave (Toamasina)
location: Toamasina (Tamatave) on Madagascar's east coast, facing the Indian Ocean, linked by rail to the capital Antananarivo.
summary: Toamasina is Madagascar's main port, run by the Société du Port à gestion Autonome de Toamasina (SPAT). Its container terminal handled 250,284 TEU in 2024, up 13.4 per cent on 2023. A USD 639 million expansion, about two-thirds funded by Japan through JICA, is building a new deep-water container quay, C4, and the first 333 m of it were handed over on 21 March 2026.
vehicleHandling: The container terminal is run by Madagascar International Container Terminal Services Ltd (MICTSL), part of ICTSI, under a concession that began in 2005 and has been extended to 2040. The port has no dedicated RoRo or car terminal. In 2012 SPAT said imported vehicles were being handled at quays poorly suited to them and proposed a combined passenger and RoRo quay for car carriers of up to 320 m, with a vehicle storage area. Current sources give no sign that it has been built. The new C4 quay, planned at 470 m, is designed for container ships of up to about 14,000 TEU.
hinterland: The port serves the whole of Madagascar, including the capital Antananarivo, which it reaches by rail.

name: Port Louis
location: Port Louis, the capital of Mauritius, on the island's north-west coast in the Indian Ocean.
summary: Port Louis handles almost all of Mauritius's seaborne trade and is a regional transhipment hub. The Mauritius Ports Authority is the landlord, and the state-owned Cargo Handling Corporation Ltd (CHCL) is the only cargo handling operator. In the 2024/25 financial year the port handled a record 496,558 TEU of container traffic (719,782 TEU of throughput including transhipment moves) and 9.8 million tonnes of cargo.
vehicleHandling: Port Louis has no dedicated car terminal. Pure car carriers are worked by CHCL at its Multi-Purpose Terminal, which handles general and bulk cargo and offers RoRo handling for cars, vans, pickups, trucks and buses, as well as lift-on lift-off handling for vehicles. The port recorded 16 pure car carrier calls in 2024/25, up from 14 the year before. Containers go through CHCL's Mauritius Container Terminal at Mer Rouge, which has an 800 m quay dredged to 16.5 m.

name: Beira
location: Beira, in Sofala Province in central Mozambique, on Sofala Bay at the mouth of the Pungwe River, reached through the dredged Macuti channel.
summary: Beira is Mozambique's second largest port. Mozambique Ports and Railways (CFM) administers it, and Cornelder de Moçambique, a joint venture between CFM and the Dutch Cornelder group, has run the container and general cargo terminals since 1998. Container volumes reached a monthly record of 42,364 TEU in October 2024.

Vehicles go through Cornelder's container terminal (645 m of quay, about 12 m depth, capacity of about 400,000 TEU a year) or its multipurpose general cargo terminal (670 m of quay, about 10 m depth). Under its extended concession Cornelder plans to raise container capacity to about 700,000 TEU a year.
hinterland: Beira is the port of the Beira Corridor, which links it by road and rail to Zimbabwe, Zambia, Malawi and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The complex handled 30.9 million tonnes in 2024, much of it mineral exports from South Africa. The concession was extended in 2024 to run until 2058, with plans to raise capacity from 37 to 54 million tonnes a year.

The terminal covers about 85,000 square metres, has about 4,150 parking bays and an annual throughput capacity of 115,000 cars, with a rail siding and road carrier bays. Car carrier lines including Höegh Autoliners, NYK, WWL, Glovis and MOL call there, and the terminal also handles transhipment.

summary: Walvis Bay is Namibia's main port, managed by the Namibian Ports Authority (Namport), with 13 commercial berths. It handles about 8 million tonnes of cargo a year. A new container terminal was commissioned in 2019.

The New Container Terminal has a 600 m quay, 16 m depth and capacity for 750,000 TEU a year. Since 1 October 2024 it has been run by Terminal Investment Namibia, an MSC subsidiary, under a 25-year concession.
