name: Port Réunion
fullName: Grand Port Maritime de La Réunion
location: The town of Le Port on the north-west coast of Réunion, a French overseas department in the Indian Ocean.
summary: Port Réunion is the island's main gateway and the busiest port in overseas France. It has operated as a Grand Port Maritime since 2013. It has two sites about 3 km apart: Port Ouest (1886), now used mainly for fishing, leisure and ship repair, and Port Est (1986), which handles all commercial cargo. In 2024 it handled 5.9 million tonnes and about 377,000 TEU, with transhipment growing strongly because CMA CGM uses it as an Indian Ocean hub.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled at Port Est's conventional goods terminal, which also takes RoRo cargo. There is no separate car terminal. The port handled 28,070 vehicles in 2024, 18 per cent fewer than in 2023. The container terminal at Port Est covers 19 hectares, has 640 m of quay and can take ships of up to 9,000 TEU.

facts.label: Port authority
facts.value: Grand Port Maritime de La Réunion

facts.label: Container terminal
facts.value: 19 ha, 640 m of quay, ships up to 9,000 TEU

name: Cape Town
location: Table Bay, next to Cape Town's city centre in the Western Cape.
summary: Cape Town is one of South Africa's main container ports, managed by Transnet National Ports Authority. It has two main basins: Ben Schoeman Dock, which holds the container terminal, and Duncan Dock, which holds the multipurpose, fresh produce, liquid bulk and cruise terminals. Strong south-easterly winds regularly halt operations in the port.
vehicleHandling: Cape Town has no dedicated car terminal. Transnet Port Terminals runs its car terminals only at Durban, Gqeberha and East London. Vehicles arriving on RoRo ships are handled at the Multipurpose Terminal in Duncan Dock, a general cargo terminal with almost 1.8 km of quay that also handles fruit, grain, steel, timber and other breakbulk. The Cape Town Container Terminal in Ben Schoeman Dock has six deep-sea berths along a 1,137 m quay dredged to 15.5 m, with a capacity of about 1 million TEU a year. In the week to 20 July 2025 it handled 19,931 TEU, its highest weekly volume since March 2019.
hinterland: The port serves Cape Town and the Western Cape, with rail and road links inland to other South African centres.

facts.label: Vehicle handling
facts.value: No dedicated car terminal. RoRo vehicles use the Multipurpose Terminal, Duncan Dock

facts.label: Container operator
facts.value: Transnet Port Terminals (Cape Town Container Terminal)

facts.label: Container terminal
facts.value: Six deep-sea berths, 1,137 m quay, 15.5 m depth, about 1 million TEU capacity

name: Durban
location: Durban, in KwaZulu-Natal on South Africa's Indian Ocean coast.
summary: Durban is South Africa's busiest port and its main container gateway, managed by Transnet National Ports Authority. Its largest container terminal, Durban Container Terminal Pier 2, has been run since January 2026 by a Transnet and ICTSI partnership under a 25-year agreement signed in December 2025, which aims to lift Pier 2's capacity from 2 million to 2.8 million TEU a year.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled at the Durban Car Terminal, operated by Transnet Port Terminals and described by its operator as sub-Saharan Africa's largest automotive terminal. In the financial year to March 2026 it handled a record 695,686 fully built units from 386 car carrier calls, well above its installed capacity of 520,000 units a year. Transnet has said it wants to raise vehicle capacity at Durban to 1 million units a year, but in March 2025 it paused to review the plan after part of the area earmarked for expansion was leased to Fresh Produce Terminals.
hinterland: Durban serves KwaZulu-Natal and most of Gauteng's sea trade, and also handles significant traffic for neighbouring countries.

facts.label: Main container terminal
facts.value: DCT Pier 2, Transnet and ICTSI partnership from January 2026, 2 million TEU capacity rising to 2.8 million

name: East London
location: At the mouth of the Buffalo River in East London, Eastern Cape. The city was officially renamed KuGompo City in early 2026.
summary: East London is South Africa's only river port and a small one, with berths for ships of about 200 m or more. Its trade is closely tied to the motor industry, above all the Mercedes-Benz plant next to the harbour, which exports most of what it builds. In July 2025 the port handled its first transhipment car carriers in 13 years.
vehicleHandling: Transnet Port Terminals runs the East London Car Terminal on the West Bank, where a four-storey parking structure with 2,800 bays is linked by road directly to the Mercedes-Benz factory. In April 2025 a R60 million upgrade of the automotive N berths and West Quay gave 550 m of quay at 10.5 m depth, able to take two car carriers over 200 m long at once, and doubled the design berth capacity to 790,000 vehicle units a year. That figure is the capacity of the berths, not of the parking area.
hinterland: The port has rail and road links to the Free State and Gauteng as well as along the coast.

facts.label: Vehicle terminal
facts.value: East London Car Terminal (Transnet Port Terminals), West Bank

facts.label: Parking
facts.value: 2,800 bays on four storeys, linked to the Mercedes-Benz plant

facts.label: Automotive berths
facts.value: 550 m of quay at 10.5 m, upgraded April 2025

name: Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha)
location: On the western side of Algoa Bay in Gqeberha (formerly Port Elizabeth), Eastern Cape, about 384 nautical miles south-west of Durban and 423 nautical miles east of Cape Town.
summary: The port of Gqeberha handles dry bulk, liquid bulk, breakbulk and vehicles, with 18 berths managed by Transnet National Ports Authority. Most of the Eastern Cape's container traffic now goes through the newer deep-water Port of Ngqura across Algoa Bay. Its car terminal is the export gateway for the Volkswagen plant at Kariega, and the Polo made up 88 per cent of vehicles exported through the port in 2024.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled at the Port Elizabeth Car Terminal, an open-area terminal on Charl Malan Quay operated by Transnet Port Terminals. In 2022 it had 5,000 parking bays, and an expansion due to finish that September was adding 3,000 more, to 8,000 bays, to raise throughput from 150,000 to 280,000 units a year. In the first seven months of the 2024/25 financial year it handled 114,041 vehicles, and in November 2024 it took the 9,100-car Höegh Aurora on its first call in Africa.
hinterland: The port serves Nelson Mandela Bay and the wider Eastern Cape, including the region's vehicle manufacturing industry.

facts.label: Vehicle terminal
facts.value: Port Elizabeth Car Terminal (Transnet Port Terminals), Charl Malan Quay

facts.label: Vehicle capacity
facts.value: 8,000 bays and 280,000 units a year planned after the 2022 expansion

name: Victoria (Port Victoria)
location: Victoria, the capital of Seychelles, on the north-east side of Mahé island in the Indian Ocean.
summary: Port Victoria is the only sizeable seaport in Seychelles and handles over 95 per cent of the country's imports and exports. The Seychelles Ports Authority runs it as a multipurpose port. About 80 per cent of its business is tied to the tuna fishing industry, including fish transhipment.
vehicleHandling: All commercial cargo, including containers and vehicles, is worked at Mahé Quay, a 370 m multipurpose quay that also serves fishing vessels, tankers and cruise ships. There is no dedicated container or vehicle terminal, and the port authority said in 2023 that it had no shore cranes. A project funded by the European Investment Bank, the French Development Agency (AFD) and the EU is extending the quay to about 600 m and dredging the channel to 16 m.

facts.label: Commercial quay
facts.value: Mahé Quay, 370 m, being extended to about 600 m

facts.label: Share of national trade
facts.value: Over 95 per cent of imports and exports

name: Jamestown
location: Jamestown, the capital of the British Overseas Territory of St Helena in the South Atlantic, with a cargo wharf in the neighbouring Rupert's Valley.
summary: St Helena has no deep-water port. For most of its history ships anchored off Jamestown, and cargo was taken ashore in lighters. A one-ship wharf in Rupert's Bay, next to Jamestown, was completed in 2016 as part of the island's airport project and now serves as the harbour.
vehicleHandling: There is no container or RoRo terminal. Sea cargo comes on the cargo ship MV Helena, which sails from Cape Town about once a month and can carry about 218 TEU. Rupert's Wharf is the island's harbour. It was first built so that supplies and construction vehicles for the airport could be landed.

facts.label: Shipping service
facts.value: MV Helena, about monthly from Cape Town

name: Limassol
location: On the south coast of Cyprus, at the city of Limassol in the eastern Mediterranean.
summary: Limassol is the main seaport of Cyprus. Its New Port opened in 1974 and became the island's principal port after Famagusta became inaccessible that year. Since privatisation in 2017, operations have been split between concessionaires, with Eurogate running the container terminal and DP World the multipurpose terminal.
vehicleHandling: DP World Limassol runs the multipurpose terminal, which it describes as the largest RoRo terminal in Cyprus, with a dedicated RoRo yard of more than 20,000 sq m operating 24 hours a day. DP World says the terminal can process up to 950 vehicles a day, and it handled 60,000 multipurpose RoRo units in 2023. RoRo lines calling at the port include Grimaldi, Neptune Lines and Salamis.
hinterland: Serves the whole of the Republic of Cyprus as the island's main cargo gateway.

facts.label: Multipurpose and RoRo operator
facts.value: DP World Limassol (25-year concession, operating since 2017)

name: Piraeus
location: On the Saronic Gulf, south-west of central Athens, Greece.
summary: Piraeus is Greece's largest port and one of the busiest container and passenger ports in the Mediterranean, handling 4.64 million TEU and 19.15 million passengers in 2025. It is run by the Piraeus Port Authority SA (PPA), in which COSCO Shipping acquired a 51% stake in 2016, later rising to 67%.
vehicleHandling: PPA's car terminal in the Keratsini-Drapetsona area operates RoRo terminals G1 and G2 around 24 hours a day, handling new vehicles for the Greek market and for transhipment to the eastern Mediterranean, Black Sea and North Africa. A 40,000 sq m expansion of Herakleous Pier, inaugurated in February 2024, took the terminal to 110,000 sq m, and PPA quotes a combined capacity of 600,000 movements a year across G1 and G2. The terminal handled 247,600 new cars in 2024, down from 317,301 in 2023.
hinterland: Serves Athens and the rest of Greece, and acts as a transhipment hub for the eastern Mediterranean and Black Sea.

name: St Peter Port
location: On the east coast of Guernsey in the Channel Islands, in the island's capital.
summary: St Peter Port is Guernsey's main harbour and its only deep-water port, handling the island's passenger ferries alongside containers, general cargo and freight trailers. It is run by Guernsey Harbours, part of the States of Guernsey Trading Assets. Bulk cargo and liquids go to the separate harbour at St Sampson's.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles arrive by roll-on roll-off ferry at the two RoRo berths on the New Jetty (1 and 2 Berth), which have a trailer park and car check-in area alongside, while containers are craned on and off at the neighbouring berths. Since 28 March 2025 Brittany Ferries has run Guernsey's ferry links from Portsmouth and Poole under a 15-year contract with the States of Guernsey, using Condor Islander, Condor Voyager and Commodore Clipper.
hinterland: Serves the island of Guernsey, with onward inter-island services to Herm, Sark and Alderney.

name: Dublin
location: At the mouth of the River Liffey on the east coast of Ireland, beside Dublin city centre.
summary: Dublin Port is Ireland's leading port and handles around two-thirds of the country's port freight. In 2024 it handled 35.2 million gross tonnes, 944,296 RoRo freight units and 885,435 TEU of container traffic. It is run by the state-owned Dublin Port Company.
vehicleHandling: Dublin handled 107,095 trade vehicles in 2024, a figure that includes cars imported through Dublin and driven on to Northern Ireland. Vehicles arrive on car carriers, on RoRo freight services and on the Irish Sea ferries, with Irish Ferries and Stena Line both sailing to Holyhead and CLDN running freight services to Rotterdam and Zeebrugge.
hinterland: Serves Dublin and much of the island of Ireland, including Northern Ireland for some vehicle imports.

name: Rosslare
location: At Rosslare Harbour in County Wexford, near the south-east tip of Ireland.
summary: Rosslare Europort is the main ferry port of south-east Ireland. It is owned and run by Iarnród Éireann, the national railway company, and direct sailings to the continent have grown strongly since Brexit. In April 2023 €350 million was allocated to expanding the port.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles arrive on RoRo ferries from Wales, with Stena Line sailing twice daily from Fishguard and Irish Ferries twice daily from Pembroke Dock, and on continental routes from Cherbourg, Dunkirk, Bilbao and Zeebrugge. Neptune Lines runs a weekly trade-car service linking Rosslare with Southampton, Santander and Le Havre on vessels carrying up to 1,800 cars.
hinterland: Serves south-east Ireland.

facts.label: Trade-car service
facts.value: Neptune Lines, weekly, via Southampton, Santander and Le Havre

name: Livorno
location: On the Ligurian Sea coast of north-western Tuscany, Italy, south of Pisa.
summary: Livorno is one of Italy's busiest ports and its leading port for new cars and forest products, with a long history as a RoRo port. Systematic car traffic began in March 1967 with imports of the Ford Cortina from Britain, and vehicle volumes peaked at 666,651 units in 2018. The port handled 29.4 million tonnes of cargo in 2024.
vehicleHandling: The port's RoRo terminal has 1,741 m of quay and 477,060 sq m of land, with space for 6,000 cars at a time and an annual capacity of 1.2 million units. The dockworkers' company CILP handles about 320,000 vehicles a year and, since August 2024, has worked new cars and Grimaldi RoRo ships from the eastern side of the Darsena Toscana. Inland, the Il Faldo vehicle park at Vicarello can hold up to 30,000 vehicles, and Livorno handled 485,190 new cars in 2024.
hinterland: Serves Tuscany and central and northern Italy, with rail links south to Salerno and Gioia Tauro for vehicles.

facts.label: Port authority
facts.value: Port System Authority of the Northern Tyrrhenian Sea

name: St Helier
location: On the south coast of Jersey in the Channel Islands, beside the island's capital.
summary: St Helier Harbour is Jersey's main port, run by Ports of Jersey, which is wholly owned by the Government of Jersey. Around 420,000 tonnes of cargo a year pass through its Elizabeth Terminal, which opened in 1989. Ports of Jersey says the RoRo trailer operation now exceeds capacity and plans to redevelop Elizabeth Harbour.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles and freight trailers roll on and off at the two RoRo berths (East and West) at Elizabeth Harbour, while containers and other lift-on lift-off cargo are handled at New North Quay. Since spring 2025 DFDS has operated Jersey's ferry services under a 15-year contract, sailing from Portsmouth and Poole as well as to St Malo.
hinterland: Serves the island of Jersey.

facts.label: RoRo berths
facts.value: East and West berths, Elizabeth Harbour

name: Valletta
location: In the Grand Harbour on Malta's east coast, between Valletta and the Three Cities, with the cargo wharves at Marsa and Kordin (Paola).
summary: The Grand Harbour at Valletta is Malta's main port for domestic cargo, RoRo traffic and cruise ships. Its multipurpose facilities are run under concession by Valletta Gateway Terminals (VGT), a subsidiary of Singapore's Portek, jointly with Malta's Tumas Group. Malta's other large port, Malta Freeport at Marsaxlokk (Birżebbuġa), is a container transhipment hub where over 96% of traffic is transhipment.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles shipped to Malta by RoRo land at the Grand Harbour, where VGT handles RoRo, cars and conventional cargo at Laboratory Wharf and Deep Water Quay. Laboratory Wharf has two secure car compounds of 10,400 sq m and 9,000 sq m, and VGT offers vehicle import, export and transhipment services there. Malta Freeport handles containers only, so cars shipped in containers may be discharged there if the carrier uses the Freeport.
hinterland: Serves Malta and Gozo.

facts.label: Grand Harbour cargo operator
facts.value: Valletta Gateway Terminals (Portek, with Tumas Group)

name: Bilbao
location: On the Abra bay in Biscay, northern Spain, with the main facilities at Santurtzi and Zierbena about 15 km west of Bilbao city.
summary: Bilbao is one of Spain's largest ports and the main port of the Basque Country, with terminals for containers, bulk, forest products, vehicles, general cargo and passengers. It has 17 km of waterfront and is run by the Bilbao Port Authority within Spain's Puertos del Estado system.
vehicleHandling: The port has RoRo facilities for car traffic, and Bergé operates vehicle and RoRo terminals there among its three Bilbao terminals, which have 256,000 sq m of storage. Bilbao is a smaller car port than others on Spain's north coast, handling 12,870 vehicles in January to August 2026. Brittany Ferries sails from Bilbao to Portsmouth and Rosslare and P&O Ferries runs a Bilbao to Zeebrugge freight service.
hinterland: Serves the Basque Country and northern Spain, and lies close to car plants in Vitoria, Pamplona, Valladolid and Zaragoza.

name: Pasajes (Pasaia)
location: In a narrow natural inlet on the Basque coast of Gipuzkoa, just east of San Sebastián and close to the French border.
summary: Pasaia is a medium-sized port that mainly serves the steel, car and paper industries of Gipuzkoa and its neighbours. Three regular RoRo lines link it with Atlantic Europe, and it is run by the Pasaia Port Authority. It ranks seventh among Spanish ports for vehicles, handling 120,663 in January to August 2026.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled at a specialist car and RoRo terminal run by Noatum UECC Terminal Pasajes, a joint venture of Noatum (AD Ports Group) and car carrier UECC. The terminal has a car silo connected directly to the ship, and cars arrive from factories by rail. UECC's car carriers export to northern Europe and the UK and bring cars back for the Spanish market, and the port also has RoRo links to Portsmouth, Zeebrugge and Cuxhaven.
hinterland: Serves Gipuzkoa, Navarre, La Rioja and south-west France.

name: Sagunto
location: On Spain's Mediterranean coast at Sagunto, north of Valencia.
summary: Sagunto is one of the three ports run by the Port Authority of Valencia (Valenciaport), which has managed it since 1985. It grew up around steel and mineral exports and is now a leading Spanish port for steel products, vehicles and natural gas.
vehicleHandling: About 50 hectares of the port are given over to vehicle logistics, with RoRo and car carrier calls from lines including Grimaldi. In March 2026 the Port Authority granted Valencia Terminal Europa a 10-year concession for a new terminal for vehicles and RoRo cargo at Central Quay 2 and South Quay 2, representing a €3.9 million investment. The port handled 60,726 vehicles in the first half of 2021.
hinterland: Serves the Valencia region and eastern Spain, with historic rail links to inland Teruel.

name: Santander
location: On the Bay of Santander in Cantabria, northern Spain, with the commercial docks at Raos south of the city.
summary: Santander is a major Spanish car port and ranks fourth in Spain for vehicle traffic, handling 244,212 vehicles in January to August 2026. Commercial activity moved to the Raos area in the second half of the 20th century, with the first Raos piers opening in 1985. The port is run by the Port Authority of Santander.
vehicleHandling: The RoRo vehicle terminal at Raos covers 600,000 sq m, with 1,000 m of berths at Raos 8 and 9 for RoRo ships and car carriers, two ramps, and rail sidings for car trains. A vertical car silo beside the berths had 9,328 spaces in operation in 2026, rising to 14,600 when complete. Car carrier lines include Wallenius Wilhelmsen, Höegh Autoliners and K Line, and Brittany Ferries sails to Portsmouth and Plymouth.
hinterland: Serves Cantabria and northern and central Spain, with car traffic from plants across the Iberian peninsula.

name: Vigo
location: On the Ría de Vigo in Pontevedra, Galicia, north-west Spain.
summary: Vigo is one of Spain's most important car ports as well as a major fishing port. It handled 648,966 new cars in 2024, the sixth-highest total in Europe, and ranks second in Spain for vehicle traffic. The port is run by the Vigo Port Authority.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled at the Bouzas RoRo terminal, which has 12 m of draught and a rail link to the Atlantic Corridor, and which shipped its 15 millionth vehicle in February 2026. Stellantis is the main automotive customer, and Bouzas has short-sea RoRo services to Nantes and Zeebrugge run by Suardíaz and UECC, plus RoRo services to the UK, France and Italy.
hinterland: Serves Galicia and north-west Spain.

name: Wallhamn
location: On the island of Tjörn in Tjörn Municipality, on Sweden's west coast north of Gothenburg.
summary: Wallhamn is a specialist RoRo port for cars, trucks, buses and industrial machinery. It was founded in 1962 with the Wallenius shipping companies and received its first ship in 1965. The Grimaldi Group bought into the port in 2004 and has been its sole owner since 2009.
vehicleHandling: The port offers 200,000 sq m of outdoor and 15,000 sq m of indoor storage, and provides pre-delivery inspection (PDI), vehicle conversion and dealer services on site. Ships of up to 9.5 m draught can berth. Wallhamn handled 71,797 new cars in 2024, down from 102,384 in 2023.
hinterland: Serves the Swedish market.

name: Aqaba
location: At the head of the Gulf of Aqaba on the Red Sea, in Jordan's Aqaba Special Economic Zone.
summary: Aqaba is Jordan's only seaport, owned by the Aqaba Development Corporation (ADC) and made up of more than 12 specialised terminals. Its container terminal, run by APM Terminals, is a transit gateway for Iraq, Syria, Saudi Arabia, the West Bank and Lebanon as well as Jordan.
vehicleHandling: RoRo cargo is handled at Aqaba New Port, the Noatum Ports Aqaba Multipurpose Terminal, which also takes general cargo, dry bulk, grain and livestock across nine berths with depths of 13 to 15 m. It is operated by the Aqaba Company for Ports Operation and Management, with operation due to transfer to AD Ports Group in 2026. Containerised cargo goes through Aqaba Container Terminal.
hinterland: Serves Jordan and transit traffic to Iraq, Syria, Saudi Arabia, the West Bank and Lebanon.

facts.label: RoRo terminal
facts.value: Noatum Ports Aqaba Multipurpose Terminal (Aqaba New Port)

name: Muscat (Port Sultan Qaboos)
location: In a natural harbour at Muttrah in Muscat Governorate, on Oman's Gulf of Oman coast.
summary: Port Sultan Qaboos opened in 1974 and was for decades Muscat's main commercial port. On 31 August 2014 the Ministry of Transport and Communications announced that it would stop commercial operations and become a cruise and tourism port, citing congested roads in Muscat. Cargo operations moved to SOHAR Port.
vehicleHandling: Cars are no longer landed at Muscat itself. Since 2014 container, general cargo and RoRo traffic for the capital has gone through SOHAR Port on the Batinah coast north-west of Muscat, where RoRo car carriers berth at the C. Steinweg Oman terminal and containers go through Hutchison Ports Sohar; Port Sultan Qaboos now handles only liquid bulk, grain, naval vessels, dhows and cruise ships. Höegh Autoliners, for example, lists Sohar and Salalah as its Omani ports and does not list Muscat, so a car booked to Muscat should be expected to arrive at Sohar and travel on by road.
hinterland: Muscat and the surrounding capital area.

facts.label: Current role
facts.value: Cruise and tourism port (commercial cargo ended from 2014)

facts.label: Actual port for cars to Muscat
facts.value: SOHAR Port (C. Steinweg Oman RoRo terminal)

name: Sohar
location: At Liwa in Al Batinah North Governorate, on Oman's Gulf of Oman coast near the Strait of Hormuz.
summary: SOHAR Port and Freezone opened in 2002 and is run by Sohar Industrial Port Company, a 50:50 joint venture between the Sultanate of Oman and the Port of Rotterdam. It is Oman's main general cargo and RoRo port since Muscat's Port Sultan Qaboos stopped commercial cargo in 2014. In 2024 it handled about 74.5 million tonnes of cargo, including 943,000 TEU of containers.
vehicleHandling: RoRo car carriers berth at the C. Steinweg Oman terminal, which has held the concession for all dry bulk, break-bulk and RoRo stevedoring at Sohar since 2004 and stores vehicles in a dedicated, CCTV-monitored area. The terminal has four berths with 960 m of quay and 16 m draft alongside, and Höegh Autoliners names it as its Sohar terminal. RoRo traffic rose 25% to 87,000 units in 2024, while containerised cars go through the Hutchison Ports Sohar container terminal.
hinterland: Serves northern Oman, including the Al Batinah region and Muscat.

facts.label: Port company
facts.value: Sohar Industrial Port Company (Oman and Port of Rotterdam, 50:50)

facts.label: RoRo terminal
facts.value: C. Steinweg Oman, 4 berths, 960 m quay, 16 m draft

name: Jeddah
location: On the Red Sea coast of western Saudi Arabia, at the city of Jeddah.
summary: Jeddah Islamic Port is Saudi Arabia's main Red Sea port and one of the largest in the Middle East, with 62 berths, 11.2 km of quays and a maximum draught of 16 m. It is owned by the Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani), with individual terminals run under concession by private operators. Its container side is led by DP World's South Container Terminal and the Red Sea Gateway Terminal (RSGT).
vehicleHandling: The port has separate general cargo and RoRo terminals, which Mawani awarded to Red Sea Gateway Terminal under a 20-year concession announced in June 2025; RSGT is consolidating them into a single multipurpose terminal that handles RoRo, general and project cargo. Across its four new Red Sea multipurpose concessions RSGT expects to handle about 710,000 RoRo units a year. Cars shipped in containers go through the container terminals, such as DP World's South Container Terminal, which has five berths, 2,550 m of quay and 18 m depth alongside.
hinterland: Serves Jeddah, Mecca and western Saudi Arabia.

facts.label: RoRo and general cargo operator
facts.value: Red Sea Gateway Terminal, 20-year concession from 2025

facts.label: Container terminal operators
facts.value: DP World (South Container Terminal), Red Sea Gateway Terminal

name: Derince
location: At Derince on the north shore of the Gulf of Izmit in Kocaeli Province, north-west Turkey.
summary: Derince is a multipurpose port in the Gulf of Izmit, formerly run by Turkish State Railways and now operated as Safiport Derince. It has container, RoRo, rail, liquid chemical and dry bulk terminals, and has one of the longest in-port rail networks in the area, with rail ferry links across the Sea of Marmara and the Black Sea.
vehicleHandling: Safiport runs a dedicated RoRo vehicle terminal and quotes a projected capacity of 700,000 to 1,000,000 vehicles a year for 2026 to 2027. The port has long been used for finished-vehicle shipments thanks to its large storage area. The Gulf of Izmit is Turkey's main vehicle export area, and Ford Otosan's Gölcük plant nearby has its own port.
hinterland: Serves the Kocaeli and wider Marmara industrial region, including the car plants around the Gulf of Izmit.

facts.label: Terminals
facts.value: Container, RoRo vehicle, rail, liquid chemical, dry bulk

facts.label: Rail ferries
facts.value: To Tekirdağ and to Black Sea ports

name: Yarimca
location: At Körfez on the north shore of the Gulf of Izmit in Kocaeli Province, north-west Turkey.
summary: Port Yarımca is a dedicated RoRo vehicle terminal owned by a joint venture of OYAK and NYK. It has the highest vehicle handling capacity in Turkey and handled 406,983 new cars in 2024. The name Yarımca is also used by other terminals in the area, including DP World Yarımca, a container port at Körfez.
vehicleHandling: The terminal covers 235,000 sq m and has a capacity of 780,000 vehicles a year and 20,000 storage slots, including a multi-storey car park. All vehicles arrive and leave by RoRo ship rather than container, and on-site services include pre-delivery inspection, car washing, heat treatment for biosecurity and a bonded warehouse. Over 70% of Turkey's finished-vehicle exports go through the Gulf of Izmit's RoRo terminals.
hinterland: Serves the Marmara region, home to most of Turkey's car manufacturing, and handles exports to the EU, US, Australia and New Zealand.

name: Halifax
location: On Halifax Harbour in Nova Scotia, on Canada's Atlantic coast.
summary: Halifax is a naturally deep, ice-free harbour able to take post-Panamax container ships, and it is closer to Europe than any other North American east coast port. It is managed by the Halifax Port Authority, a federal Crown corporation, and handled 546,691 TEU of containers in 2019. Its main container terminals are South End (PSA Halifax) and Fairview Cove (Cerescorp).
vehicleHandling: Ro-ro vehicles are handled at Autoport in Eastern Passage, on the east side of the harbour, a vehicle processing and transshipment facility wholly owned by CN Rail. It handles nearly 185,000 vehicles a year (reported in 2024), virtually all from European manufacturers, and offers pre-delivery inspection, servicing and accessory fitting before onward delivery by truck and rail. Autoport also handles almost all new vehicle deliveries to Newfoundland.
hinterland: Atlantic Canada, with direct access to the Canadian National rail network.

name: Vancouver
location: On the coast of British Columbia around Burrard Inlet and the Fraser River, in the Vancouver metropolitan area.
summary: The Port of Vancouver is Canada's largest port and one of the largest in North America by tonnage, handling 141 million metric revenue tonnes in 2022. It is run by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority and comprises 29 deep-sea and domestic marine terminals stretching from Burrard Inlet along the Fraser River.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled at the Annacis Auto Terminal on Annacis Island in Delta, on the Fraser River, operated by Wallenius Wilhelmsen. An upgrade completed in July 2025 merged the former Richmond Auto Terminal into Annacis, raising capacity to up to 480,000 vehicles a year and adding 60 rail car spots and a new vehicle processing building. The port imported nearly 470,000 vehicles in 2024.

name: Altamira
location: On Mexico's Gulf of Mexico coast in Altamira, Tamaulipas, about 15 nautical miles north of Tampico.
summary: Altamira is an industrial port complex that began operating in 1985 and has 17 berths and 14 marine terminals. It handles over 22 million tonnes of cargo a year and has grown quickly as a vehicle port, moving 515,077 vehicles in 2024, up 12.6% on 2023. Most of that traffic is exports.
vehicleHandling: AMPORTS runs a 70-hectare automotive terminal at Altamira, in operation since 1997, with ro-ro handling, rail loading, vehicle processing, pre-delivery inspection and a body and paint shop; it processed about 294,000 of the port's vehicles in 2024. Altamira Terminal Portuaria also handles vehicles. In the first four months of 2024 more than 98% of the port's vehicle traffic was exports, with imports around 3,000 units.

name: Lázaro Cárdenas
location: On Mexico's Pacific coast in Lázaro Cárdenas, Michoacán.
summary: Lázaro Cárdenas is a deep-water port and one of Mexico's largest, handling containers, minerals, bulk and vehicles, with rail service provided by Canadian Pacific Kansas City. It is Mexico's main Pacific gateway for vehicles, handling 675,385 vehicles in 2024 (down 3.4% on 2023's 699,133).
vehicleHandling: The Terminal Especializada de Automóviles (TEA) is operated by SSA México, and vehicles are also handled at the port's multi-use terminals, with Hyundai Glovis and AMPORTS developing their own vehicle yards. More than 50 vehicle brands use the port, and it has become the main entry point for new vehicles from China and other Asian countries on Mexico's Pacific coast.
hinterland: Mexico and the US, with the CPKC rail line running north from the port; it is a gateway for Asian cargo bound for US markets.

name: Manzanillo
location: On Mexico's Pacific coast in Manzanillo, in the state of Colima.
summary: Manzanillo is Mexico's largest container port, with capacity of about 3.7 million TEU in 2023 and more than 1.8 million TEU handled in the first half of 2024. It is the principal Pacific entry point for imports bound for central Mexico, and a government expansion programme aims to lift capacity to 10 million TEU by 2030.
vehicleHandling: Manzanillo is primarily a container port and carries little ro-ro vehicle traffic: it handled 1,039 vehicles in 2024, down 75.6% on 2023, while Mexico's Pacific vehicle trade is concentrated at Lázaro Cárdenas and Mazatlán. For vehicle shipments it is therefore mainly relevant as a container port.
hinterland: Central Mexico, including the Mexico City area.

name: Veracruz
location: On Mexico's Gulf of Mexico coast in the city of Veracruz, in Veracruz state.
summary: Veracruz is Mexico's oldest port, dating from the founding of Villa Rica de la Vera Cruz in 1519, and was the main commercial hub of New Spain. Today it is Mexico's busiest vehicle port, handling 850,772 vehicles in 2024, and it is linked by toll highway and rail to Puebla and Mexico City.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled by two terminal operators, CPV (CSI Group) and SSA México, across seven ro-ro berths and storage for more than 53,000 vehicles. SSA's automobile terminal comprises Patio Norte (9.5 hectares, 4,000 units) and Yard 5 (8.6 hectares, 5,000 units), with washing, inspection, repair and rail and truck transfer services. Five public yards added in 2024 provided nearly 33,000 extra parking spaces.
hinterland: Central Mexico, including Puebla and Mexico City, served by the Ferrosur and Kansas City Southern de México (now CPKC) rail networks.

name: Baltimore
aliases: Helen Delich Bentley Port of Baltimore
location: On the Patapsco River in Baltimore, Maryland, on the upper north-west shore of Chesapeake Bay.
summary: Baltimore is one of the leading US ports for ro-ro cargo and handled 45.9 million tons of cargo worth $62.2 billion in 2024, despite the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse in March 2024 closing the channel for about 11 weeks. It is run by the Maryland Port Administration and lies within an overnight drive of two-thirds of the US population.
vehicleHandling: Autos and other ro-ro cargo are handled at the state-owned Dundalk Marine Terminal, with nearly 200 acres of ro-ro pavement, and the Fairfield Marine Terminal, as well as at private terminals. Baltimore handled 749,799 cars and light trucks in 2024, second in the US, and ranked first for ro-ro farm and construction machinery. Ro-ro carriers calling include Wallenius Wilhelmsen, Höegh Autoliners and MOL.
hinterland: The Mid-Atlantic and US Midwest; Baltimore is closer to Midwest manufacturing centres than other East Coast ports.

name: Benicia
location: In Benicia, in California's San Francisco Bay Area.
summary: The Port of Benicia is a privately owned vehicle terminal operated by AMPORTS, which also acts as the port authority. It is Northern California's main vehicle import point, processing about 240,000 finished vehicles in 2024, many from South Korea, Japan, China and Vietnam, plus short-sea traffic from Mexico.
vehicleHandling: AMPORTS runs the terminal on 98 acres of yard with three private berths, a dynamic capacity of about 400,000 cars and a 356,000 sq ft vehicle processing centre offering ro-ro handling, EV charging, accessory fitting, body shop and mechanical work. It handles both new vehicles and privately owned vehicles. General Motors and Toyota are among its largest customers.
hinterland: Northern California, with Union Pacific rail next to the terminal and truck access via Interstate 80.

name: Brunswick
location: On the Atlantic coast of Georgia at Brunswick.
summary: Brunswick is run by the Georgia Ports Authority and is the busiest US gateway for ro-ro cargo, ranked the nation's top auto port for two consecutive years. Georgia Ports completed $284 million of self-financed improvements at Brunswick in fiscal year 2025.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled at Colonel's Island Terminal, which has three deepwater ro-ro berths, a fourth $100 million berth under construction, four on-terminal auto processors and around 1,700 acres of operational storage. In fiscal year 2025 (July 2024 to June 2025) the terminal moved more than 871,000 auto units and over 27,200 units of heavy machinery. Its Southside rail yard has been expanded to 10 trains a week.

name: Charleston
location: In Charleston, South Carolina, at Charleston Harbor.
summary: Charleston is owned and operated by the South Carolina Ports Authority and is one of the leading container ports on the US East Coast, handling 2.85 million TEU in fiscal year 2022. At 52 feet at mean low tide it has the deepest harbour on the East Coast.
vehicleHandling: Ro-ro and breakbulk cargo is handled at Columbus Street Terminal on the Cooper River, a 155-acre site with 3,500 feet of berth for up to five ships and 44.3 acres of ro-ro storage, served by CSX and Norfolk Southern rail. Ro-ro operations moved there from Union Pier in 2011, largely to handle BMW exports from its Spartanburg plant, which arrive by rail.
hinterland: South Carolina and the south-east US, including BMW's Spartanburg plant.

name: Davisville
location: In the Quonset Business Park at North Kingstown, Rhode Island, on Narragansett Bay.
summary: The Port of Davisville is run by the Quonset Development Corporation and is one of the top 10 auto import ports in North America, receiving more than 200,000 vehicles a year. It has five terminals with 4,500 ft of berthing, 235 acres of operating area, on-dock rail and a 150-tonne mobile harbour crane. A new Terminal 5 Pier, the first new pier at Quonset in more than 70 years, received its first ship in May 2026.
vehicleHandling: Imported vehicles are processed at the port by NORAD (North Atlantic Distribution), a private company that has handled more than 5 million vehicles in total, before distribution to dealers across the north-east. Car carriers use Pier 1, Pier 2 and the Terminal 5 Pier, all dredged to 32 ft MLLW; the first ship at Terminal 5, the ro-ro Viking Odesa, landed more than 1,100 GM and Chevrolet trucks and SUVs in May 2026.
hinterland: New England and the north-east US.

facts.label: Depth
facts.value: 32 ft MLLW at Pier 1, Pier 2 and Terminal 5

name: Galveston
location: At the mouth of Galveston Bay on the Texas Gulf Coast, about 30 minutes' steaming from the open sea.
summary: The Port of Galveston, also known as Galveston Wharves, handles bulk, breakbulk, ro-ro, project and container cargo as well as a large cruise business. It handled 3.4 million tons of cargo in 2024, of which ro-ro accounted for 445,000 tons.
vehicleHandling: Ro-ro cargo, mainly new cars and heavy equipment, is handled at the West Port Cargo Complex, including ro-ro berths at Piers 30-32 and 39/40, with Ports America Texas as stevedore. Wallenius Wilhelmsen has called since 1995, and ARC, K Line and NYK also run services, giving six to ten ro-ro calls a month. The port is investing $77.5 million to expand the West Port Cargo Complex.

facts.label: Ro-ro carriers
facts.value: Wallenius Wilhelmsen, ARC, K Line, NYK

name: Jacksonville
location: On the St Johns River in Jacksonville, north-east Florida.
summary: JAXPORT is run by the Jacksonville Port Authority and is Florida's largest container port as well as one of the leading US vehicle ports. It has three cargo terminals, Blount Island, Dames Point and Talleyrand, and offers same-day truck access to about 98 million US consumers.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled at Blount Island Marine Terminal, which has two dedicated ro-ro berths, and at Dames Point Marine Terminal, with AMPORTS and Southeast Toyota Distributors as the auto processors. Together they moved more than 509,000 vehicles in 2024. A $60 million programme has lengthened Berth 22 at Blount Island to take vehicle carriers of about 750 feet, with a new vehicle berth due in early 2027.
hinterland: Florida and the south-east US.

name: Long Beach
location: In Long Beach, southern California.
summary: Long Beach is one of the busiest container ports in the US and a major gateway for trade with Asia, handling 9.7 million TEU in 2024. It is run by the City of Long Beach Harbor Department under a five-member Board of Harbor Commissioners, and the Alameda Corridor rail line links it to inland rail yards.
vehicleHandling: The main vehicle facility is Toyota Logistics Services at Pier B, a site of more than 117 acres that Toyota has occupied for over 40 years. It receives about 200,000 new Toyota and Lexus vehicles a year (2024), fits accessories and sends them on by rail and truck, and is Toyota's largest vehicle processing facility in North America.
hinterland: Southern California, with rail links to the rest of the US.

facts.label: Port authority
facts.value: Harbor Department of the City of Long Beach

name: New York
fullName: Port of New York and New Jersey
location: In New York Harbor, with its main cargo terminals at Port Newark, Elizabeth and Bayonne in New Jersey and on Staten Island and in Brooklyn.
summary: The Port of New York and New Jersey is the largest port on the US East Coast, overseen by the bi-state Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. It handled 8,698,526 TEU in 2024 and 8,897,531 TEU in 2025. It moved 410,092 autos in 2024, and auto volume fell by 11% in 2025.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled at the Port Newark and Elizabeth complex and at Port Jersey in Jersey City and Bayonne, with Maher Terminals and Ports America as auto stevedores. Processing is done by FAPS at Port Newark, part of Ports America, with capacity for more than 500,000 vehicles a year, the Toyota Motor Logistics Center at Port Newark, and BMW's Port Jersey Vehicle Preparation Center. Some 18,858 autos moved by rail in 2024.
hinterland: The New York metropolitan area and the north-east US, with rail links via Norfolk Southern, CSX and Canadian Pacific.

facts.label: Port authority
facts.value: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey

name: Norfolk
location: In Hampton Roads, south-east Virginia, with terminals in Norfolk, Portsmouth and Newport News.
summary: The Port of Virginia is owned by the Virginia Port Authority and operated by its affiliate Virginia International Terminals. Its largest terminal is Norfolk International Terminals, and the Hampton Roads harbour handled 3,523,512 TEU in calendar 2024, while the authority's terminals moved about 3.4 million TEU in the fiscal year to June 2025.
vehicleHandling: Ro-ro cargo is handled mainly at Newport News Marine Terminal on the north bank of the James River, the port's main break-bulk and ro-ro facility, with 165 acres, four berths totalling 3,480 ft, 41 ft of water, more than 60 acres of open storage and direct on-dock CSX rail. CP&O, a joint venture of The Cooper Group, Ports America and SSA Marine, handles automobiles there. The port does not publish a separate ro-ro or vehicle unit count.
hinterland: Virginia and the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest, with rail links via Norfolk Southern and CSX.

facts.label: Ro-ro terminal
facts.value: Newport News Marine Terminal, 4 berths, 3,480 ft, 41 ft depth

name: Port Hueneme
location: In Port Hueneme, Ventura County, California, between Los Angeles and San Francisco.
summary: The Port of Hueneme is run by the Oxnard Harbor District and is the only commercial deep-water port between Los Angeles and San Francisco. It shares the harbour with Naval Base Ventura County, and is one of the top 10 US ports for both vehicles and fresh produce.
vehicleHandling: The port has a dedicated ro-ro terminal with six deepwater berths and 8,000 parking bays, next to three vehicle processors: Wallenius Wilhelmsen Solutions, Glovis America and BMW. The port states it handles more than 375,000 vehicles a year and over 6% of US car volume, and vehicles provide about 60% of its operating income.
hinterland: Southern and Central California, reached via US 101 and the Ventura County Railroad to Union Pacific.

facts.label: Vehicle processors
facts.value: Wallenius Wilhelmsen Solutions; Glovis America; BMW

facts.label: Rail
facts.value: Ventura County Railroad to Union Pacific

name: San Diego
location: On San Diego Bay in southern California, about 10 miles from the Mexican border.
summary: The Port of San Diego is run by the San Diego Unified Port District, created in 1962, which manages the bay across five cities. It has two cargo terminals: Tenth Avenue Marine Terminal for refrigerated and breakbulk cargo, and National City Marine Terminal for vehicles.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled at National City Marine Terminal, a 135-acre site with four working berths, operated by Pasha Automotive Services under a terminal agreement running to 2040. The port says it handles one in every ten new foreign cars shipped to the US, and Pasha reported volumes of more than 400,000 vehicles a year when the agreement was signed in 2010.
hinterland: Southern California, with direct Class I rail access at National City.

name: Tacoma
location: On Commencement Bay at Tacoma, Washington, at the southern end of Puget Sound.
summary: The Port of Tacoma has run its marine cargo business jointly with the Port of Seattle since 2015 as the Northwest Seaport Alliance, which handled 3,156,598 TEU in 2025, down 5.5% on 2024. Automobiles are among Tacoma's main imports, and the alliance recorded 269 ro-ro vessel calls in 2025.
vehicleHandling: Car carriers berth at East Blair One (EB1) in Tacoma, a 26-acre auto and break-bulk terminal with a 1,200 ft berth, 51 ft of water and an on-dock rail spur, used by carriers including EUKOR, Hyundai Glovis, Wallenius Wilhelmsen, K Line, MOL and NYK. Imported vehicles are processed at the 146-acre Marshall Avenue Auto Facility, operated by Auto Warehousing Company with near-dock rail. Auto volumes at NWSA and Port of Tacoma facilities were 274,186 units in 2025, down 18.8% on 2024; no separate Tacoma-only figure is published.
hinterland: The Pacific Northwest, with rail links to the US Midwest.

facts.value: Auto Warehousing Company, Marshall Avenue Auto Facility (146 acres)

name: Brisbane
location: At the mouth of the Brisbane River on Fisherman Islands, a reclaimed site in Moreton Bay east of Brisbane, Queensland.
summary: Queensland's main container and general cargo port, managed by Port of Brisbane Pty Ltd under a 99-year lease from the Queensland Government. It has 27 operating berths and more than 8,200 metres of quayline, and moves more than 28 million tonnes of cargo a year.
vehicleHandling: Car carriers are worked at the AAT Fisherman Islands terminal, a 26-hectare multi-purpose facility at Berths 1 to 3 (696 metres of quay, up to 14 metres deep) handling motor vehicles, RoRo, breakbulk and containers. AAT says its Fisherman Islands and Port Kembla terminals together handle more than 600,000 vehicles a year. Containers are handled at three terminals run by DP World (Berths 4 to 7), Patrick (Berths 8 to 10) and Brisbane Container Terminals, a Hutchison business (Berths 11 and 12).
hinterland: Brisbane and south-east Queensland.

facts.value: Port of Brisbane Pty Ltd (99-year lease)

facts.value: DP World, Patrick, Brisbane Container Terminals

facts.label: Cargo
facts.value: More than 28 million tonnes a year

name: Fremantle
location: At the mouth of the Swan River in Fremantle, about 20 km south-west of central Perth, Western Australia.
summary: Western Australia's main general cargo and container port, run by Fremantle Ports, a Western Australian government trading enterprise. The Inner Harbour at Fremantle handles containers, vehicle imports, livestock and cruise ships, while the Outer Harbour at Kwinana handles bulk cargo. The first container ship to reach Australia, Encounter Bay from the United Kingdom, docked here in March 1969.
vehicleHandling: Car carriers and RoRo ships berth in the Inner Harbour, which recorded 19 RoRo and car carrier calls in August 2025, when 10,142 new and 2,104 used vehicles were imported. Containers are handled at two terminals on North Quay, operated by DP World and Patrick. The Inner Harbour handled 892,204 TEU in calendar year 2024.
hinterland: Perth and Western Australia.

facts.label: Container terminals
facts.value: DP World and Patrick, North Quay

name: Melbourne
location: At the mouth of the Yarra River at the head of Port Phillip Bay, beside central Melbourne, Victoria.
summary: Australia's largest port for containerised and general cargo, handling 3.39 million TEU in the 2024-25 financial year. Its commercial operations were leased in 2016 to the Lonsdale Consortium for 50 years and are run by Port of Melbourne Operations.
vehicleHandling: Vehicles are handled at the automotive and RoRo terminal at Webb Dock West, developed by MIRRAT (Melbourne International RoRo and Automotive Terminal), a Wallenius Wilhelmsen Logistics subsidiary, and opened in April 2016 with a design throughput of one million units a year. The port handled 386,402 new motor vehicle units in the 2024-25 financial year. Containers are handled at Swanson Dock by DP World and Patrick, and at Webb Dock East by Victoria International Container Terminal (VICT).
hinterland: Melbourne and Victoria.

facts.label: Operator
facts.value: Port of Melbourne Operations (50-year lease from 2016)

facts.label: Container terminals
facts.value: DP World, Patrick (Swanson Dock); VICT (Webb Dock East)

name: Port Kembla (Sydney)
location: In the Illawarra region of New South Wales, just east of Wollongong, about 90 km south of Port Botany and 67 km from south-west Sydney.
summary: A deep-water port founded in the late 1890s to export Illawarra coal, now run commercially by NSW Ports with the Port Authority of New South Wales responsible for harbour operations. Besides vehicles it handles coal, grain, bulk liquids, steel and general cargo, and it is approved as the state's next container port once Port Botany nears capacity.
vehicleHandling: Port Kembla handles all of New South Wales's motor vehicle imports, which moved here from Sydney Harbour in 2007. Australian Amalgamated Terminals (AAT), Australia's largest motor vehicle and RoRo terminal operator, runs four berths (103, 105, 106 and 107) in two terminals in the Inner Harbour, with a total quay length of 910 metres. AAT says its Port Kembla and Brisbane terminals together handle more than 600,000 vehicles a year.
hinterland: Sydney and New South Wales.

facts.label: Harbour authority
facts.value: Port Authority of New South Wales

name: Suva
location: On Suva Harbour on the south-east coast of Viti Levu, serving Fiji's capital city.
summary: Fiji's largest and busiest international port, regulated by Fiji Ports Corporation Limited, with cargo handled by its subsidiary Fiji Ports Terminal Limited. Its main facility, Kings Wharf, was begun in 1912 and was rebuilt to a seismic-resistant design in a rehabilitation completed in October 2005.
vehicleHandling: Suva is Fiji's car carrier port: Fiji Ports Corporation recorded 32 car carrier calls at Suva in 2023 and 39 in 2022, against none at Lautoka, plus 24 combined roll-on roll-off and container general cargo calls in 2023. Large vessels berth at the 496 metre Kings Wharf, with Walu Bay as a cross berth for ships under 9 metres draft, and cargo handling at both is by Fiji Ports Terminal Limited.
hinterland: Suva and south-east Viti Levu.

name: Lautoka
location: At Lautoka on the west coast of Viti Levu, in Fiji's Ba Province.
summary: Fiji's second-largest port and the main maritime gateway for western Viti Levu, regulated by Fiji Ports Corporation Limited. It is the country's main bulk port, handling sugar, molasses, woodchips, petroleum and gas, and it is also a base for inter-island cruise operators.
vehicleHandling: Lautoka has no dedicated vehicle terminal, and Fiji Ports Corporation recorded no car carrier calls there in 2021, 2022 or 2023. Ships work at the 295 metre Queens Wharf and North Quay, with cargo handled by Fiji Ports Terminal Limited, and the main berths take vessels drawing up to 11 metres.
hinterland: Western Viti Levu, including Lautoka, Fiji's second-largest urban area.

name: Papeete
location: At Papeete on the north-west coast of Tahiti, in the Society Islands.
summary: French Polynesia's only international port and the hub for redistribution to the outer islands, run by the Port autonome de Papeete, a public body created in 1962 that also manages facilities on Moorea and Raiatea. The port says it handles 90% of the territory's imported goods. In 2025 it handled 1.45 million tonnes and 84,062 TEU of containers, with 990 ship calls at the commercial port.
vehicleHandling: International cargo is worked at the international commerce terminal on Motu Uta, a reclaimed former islet, where a 453 metre deep-sea quay with three berths takes container ships and general cargo vessels and 140,000 square metres of yard hold containers and break-bulk. At the terminal entrance a four-level vehicle storage building holds 500 vehicles, beside a 3,700 square metre area with 130 spaces for heavy and oversized equipment, and loading and discharge is carried out by private stevedoring companies. Roll-on roll-off cargo came to 14,240 tonnes in 2025.
hinterland: Tahiti and the islands of French Polynesia.

facts.label: Deep-sea quay
facts.value: 453 m, three berths, at Motu Uta

name: Nouméa
location: On a sheltered deep-water harbour on a peninsula at the south of Grande Terre, New Caledonia's main island.
summary: New Caledonia's chief port, run by the Port autonome de la Nouvelle-Calédonie, a public industrial and commercial body that also manages the port of Wé on Lifou. Traffic recovered in 2025, rising 4.4% to 3.88 million tonnes, while containers fell 2.3% to 76,038 TEU.
vehicleHandling: There is no dedicated vehicle terminal. Cars arrive at the commercial quay (Quai de commerce, or Grand Quai) on the Grande Rade, which takes vessels of up to 250 metres and 10.5 metres draft, and loading and discharge are carried out by four private stevedores: Groupe Nouméa Port, Manutrans, SAT and SATO. Imports of light vehicles fell 67% to 1,773 units in 2025, and a further 250 metre berth, Poste 8, is planned for the commercial quay.
hinterland: Nouméa and New Caledonia.

name: Auckland
location: On the Waitematā Harbour beside central Auckland, on New Zealand's North Island.
summary: New Zealand's largest commercial port, owned by Auckland Council and built largely on 55 hectares of reclaimed land. In the year to 30 June 2026 it handled 932,209 TEU and 202,555 vehicles.
vehicleHandling: RoRo ships and car carriers are worked at the multi-cargo wharves in the middle of the port, including Captain Cook, Bledisloe, Marsden, Freyberg and Jellicoe, with stevedoring by third-party companies. A five-storey car handling building on Bledisloe Wharf, completed in 2020, stores imported cars and was designed for unloading at 200 cars an hour. Containers are handled at the Fergusson container terminal.
hinterland: Auckland and the upper North Island.

facts.label: Car handling
facts.value: Multi-cargo wharves and Bledisloe car handling building

name: Lyttelton
location: In Lyttelton Harbour on Banks Peninsula, linked to Christchurch, about 12 km away, by a road tunnel through the Port Hills.
summary: The South Island's largest port, run by Lyttelton Port Company, which is owned by Christchurch City Holdings on behalf of Christchurch City Council. It is home to New Zealand's largest coal export facility and handles containers, bulk fuel, logs and imported cars.
vehicleHandling: Imported cars are handled as conventionally stevedored cargo on the port's wharves, and Lyttelton Port Company handled 39,138 vehicles in the year to 30 June 2026. Containers are handled at the Cashin Quay container terminal, which moved 427,462 TEU in the same year, with inland ports at CityDepot in Christchurch and MidlandPort in Rolleston.
hinterland: Christchurch, Canterbury and the wider South Island.

name: Nelson
location: In the city of Nelson on Tasman Bay, at the top of New Zealand's South Island.
summary: The international port for the top of the South Island, run by Port Nelson Limited, which is owned through Infrastructure Holdings Limited by Nelson City Council and Tasman District Council. It handled 3.8 million tonnes of cargo in the year to 30 June 2026, mostly exports of logs and other forestry products, seafood, fruit and wine. In the year to June 2025 it handled 106,400 TEU of containers and 675 vessel visits.
vehicleHandling: Port Nelson is a shallow tidal port with four principal cargo berths, Main Wharf (300 m), Brunt Quay (190 m), McGlashen Quay (330 m) and Kingsford Quay (170 m), which between them serve container ships, car carriers, log ships, bulk carriers and tankers. New and second-hand vehicles are one of its main imports, and the port company provides the stevedoring. It does not publish vehicle numbers, but reported that vehicle imports fell 47% in the year to June 2025.
hinterland: Nelson, Tasman and Marlborough.

facts.value: Main Wharf, Brunt Quay, McGlashen Quay, Kingsford Quay
